suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of HAXcms utility/auth modules (particularly function definitions around line 2160) and config files storing HMAC keys. Correlate with subsequent token-forgery requests to the same target using the extracted key.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: JWT Signature Validation Failures or Admin-Claim Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'forge arbitrary admin-level JSON Web Tokens'. No pipeline UC detected this privilege-escalation indicator. Detection must target JWT validation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HAXcms logs JWT signature validation failures or when admin-role claims appear in request contexts (user IDs, source IPs, timestamps) that violate admin-user baselines. Threshold: 3+ validation failures from same source within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: State-Changing Requests to Protected Admin Endpoints via Forged Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact phase: 'full admin access with a single HTTP request' to protected endpoints. No UC detected unauthorized state changes (POST/PUT/DELETE) initiated by non-admin or external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH to {saveOutline,saveManifest,saveNode,createSite,deleteSite,saveFile,saveUser} endpoints where requester is either unauthenticated, external-sourced, or claims non-admin roles. Enforce that these endpoints require valid admin JWT with matching request pattern.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Automated Extraction of /system/api/connectionSettings from Unknown Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article attack vector: 'unauthenticated attacker' retrieving '/system/api/connectionSettings' to extract HMAC key. This is reconnaissance + exploitation. Pipeline generated no phase entries for exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-frequency or repeated GET requests to /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint from unknown/external source IPs with successful (200) responses. Baseline legitimate polling; alert when request rate or source diversity deviates.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Package Version Inventory — @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs < 25.0.1
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable package version constraint. Pipeline extraction returned empty IOCs{}. Threat actor would target systems with <=25.0.0; detection via software inventory is first-line defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory scan for presence of @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs versions 0.0.1 through 25.0.0 across Node.js package managers (npm, yarn, pnpm lock files) and runtime package-list inspection. Flag for immediate patching to 25.0.1+.

suggestion.title: HAXcms: Sequential Exploitation Chain Correlation — GET key + POST admin (Forged JWT)
suggestion.rationale: Two-step attack sequence described in article: step 1='extract HMAC key', step 2='forge JWT + admin write'. No pipeline UC explicitly correlated both phases in single detection. UC_33_3 attempted this but conflated with file-system noise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when same source IP executes GET /system/api/connectionSettings with 200 response, followed within 5 minutes by POST/PUT/DELETE to any admin endpoint, especially if request patterns suggest automated tooling (identical user-agent, sub-second inter-request timing, rapid endpoint enumeration).

suggestion.title: Malicious npm package installation (@opensearch-project/opensearch 3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, 3.8.0)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'external actor gaining force-push permissions...to embed malicious packages into four release versions.' UC_35_2 fully provided in article with Splunk and Defender KQL but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe, yarn.exe, pnpm.exe, npx.exe execution for installation of @opensearch-project/opensearch with versions 3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, or 3.8.0 in command line. Alert on exact version matches as they represent delivery of known-compromised package.

suggestion.title: Postinstall script execution from malicious OpenSearch package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious payload embedded in npm package; UC_35_5 explicitly provided in article but pipeline failed to extract. Malware executes via postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by node.exe or npm.exe where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains @opensearch-project/opensearch and child process spawns cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash, curl, wget, certutil, or bitsadmin.

suggestion.title: On-disk presence of malicious OpenSearch payload by file hash
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three SHA256 hashes under 'Indicators of Compromise (high-fidelity only).' UC_35_3 with complete KQL and Splunk provided but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DeviceFileEvents where SHA256 matches any of the three malicious hashes. Correlate with node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch directory paths to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: C2 beacon to Mini Shai-Hulud/TeamPCP domains (api.masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, *.getsession.org)
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_35_4 title attributes C2 to Mini Shai-Hulud/TeamPCP and lists four malicious domains. Complete detection with Splunk and Defender KQL provided but pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections for api.masscan.cloud, git-tanstack.com, filev2.getsession.org, seed1.getsession.org. Correlate with systems matching OpenSearch installation detection window (2026-05-12 onwards).

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration over C2 channel
suggestion.rationale: Article includes T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel) and T1568 (Dynamic Resolution) in MITRE technique list but no explicit exfiltration hunt provided. Likely phase following successful C2 establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume or anomalous data transfers egressing to the four C2 domains, particularly DNS exfiltration patterns (high-entropy subdomains, base32/base64 encoding) or suspicious HTTP GET/POST parameters containing encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45829 Exploitation Attempt via Model Settings Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'attacker can send a crafted request to force ChromaDB to load a malicious model' with embedded settings before authentication. No detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChromaDB API endpoints for POST/PUT requests containing model configuration parameters (trust_remote_code, model_name, repo_id) sent to endpoints marked as requiring authentication. Correlate with subsequent child process spawning or outbound connections to huggingface.co domain within 2 seconds of request receipt.

suggestion.title: Hugging Face Model Load Before Authentication Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authentication is only performed after that step, bypassing security' and 'by the time it fires, the model has already been fetched and executed.' No detection for out-of-order authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections from ChromaDB process (python/fastapi) to huggingface.co (resolver.huggingface.co, cdn-lfs.huggingface.co) that occur without prior successful HTTP 200 response from /auth or /verify endpoints. Track model artifact downloads >10MB in absence of valid session token.

suggestion.title: ChromaDB HTTP 500 Response Following Model Load Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes end-state: 'The server rejects the request, returns a 500, and the attacker's payload has already run.' This is the forensic signature post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 500 responses from ChromaDB API endpoints with prior model-loading requests (high entropy repo_id parameters, trust_remote_code=true) and subsequent unexpected child process creation (git, python, bash) or file writes in /tmp or process-owned directories within 1 second of 500 response.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ChromaDB Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'was introduced in ChromaDB 1.0.0 and was unpatched in version 1.5.8' and deployment risk affects '73% of internet-exposed instances.' Pipeline should flag deployments by version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ChromaDB processes or container images with version strings 1.0.0 through 1.5.8 via pip show, pip list, requirements.txt parsing, or Dockerfile inspection. Flag any exposed over HTTP via netstat/ss listening on port 8000 (default) or via AWS/GCP public IP enumeration.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed ChromaDB API Server Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'the PyPI package...is at risk when servers are accessible over HTTP' and cites Shodan data: '73% of internet-exposed instances are running vulnerable version.' No discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for ChromaDB FastAPI services listening on 0.0.0.0:8000 or publicly routable IPs. Check HTTP response headers for 'uvicorn', 'fastapi', or X-Powered-By: FastAPI. Correlate with presence of vulnerable version 1.0.0–1.5.8 and log unauthenticated POST/GET requests to /api/v1/* endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious Model Download from Hugging Face During ChromaDB Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'attacker can send a crafted request to force ChromaDB to load a malicious model from the Hugging Face platform and execute it locally.' Network-level model retrieval is the attack transport.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to huggingface.co/*/resolve/main or cdn-lfs.huggingface.co initiated by ChromaDB process without corresponding user-initiated deployment workflow. Flag concurrent downloads >50MB + child process spawning (git clone, python -m, bash, curl) as post-download artifact staging.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Version Detection (npm/PyPI/gem)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions '5 Supply Chain Attacks in 48 Hours' — all supply-chain attacks involve poisoned package releases with specific version strings that differ from legitimate upstream. Pipeline should extract exact package@version IOCs and generate install-time detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager commands (npm install, pip install, gem install, go get) and node_modules/site-packages writes for known-malicious package@version combinations. Baseline legitimate versions from upstream registry metadata; flag installations matching attacker-published versions within 48-72 hour window of legitimate release.

suggestion.title: Registry Credential Compromise & Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks require publishing access to official registries (npm, PyPI, RubyGems). Article describes '5 attacks in 48 hours' requiring rapid account compromises or token theft. Pipeline missed detection for registry auth token exfiltration, credential stuffing against npm/PyPI, or session hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for: (1) npm/PyPI authentication tokens in environment variables, git configs, or process memory; (2) failed authentication attempts against npm, PyPI, or RubyGems APIs from unusual geolocations or non-CI principals; (3) TOTP/2FA bypass attempts or unusual session reuse patterns within 48 hours of package publication.

suggestion.title: Artifact Tampering & Supply Chain Repository Mutation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks mutate git repositories, package manifests, or build artifacts. Article describes multiple attacks — each requires code injection or manifest manipulation. Pipeline did not identify detection for unauthorized commits, webhook modifications, or CI/CD pipeline poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits authored by non-standard principals, commits outside business hours or from unusual geos, modifications to package.json/setup.py/Gemfile without corresponding PR review, or git hook installation in repository roots. Baseline maintainer commit patterns per repository and alert on significant deviation.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article context: securing 'one layer' is insufficient. Most supply-chain attacks succeed because transitive dependencies are installed without scrutiny. Pipeline should generate detection for unexpected dependency resolution, version downgrades, or introduction of new transitive dependencies not present in lock files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package lock files (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, Pipfile.lock) before/after install. Alert if resolved versions do not match pinned versions, if new transitive dependencies appear without corresponding package.json changes, or if dependency count increases >5% between builds. Correlate with registry API queries for version enumeration.

suggestion.title: C2 Egress to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain payloads steal credentials, exfiltrate secrets, or establish persistence via C2. Article mentions multiple attacks — each likely includes exfiltration or persistence callback. Pipeline did not generate detection for network connections to known C2 domains or unusual HTTPS/DNS egress from build/runtime environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and network connections from CI/CD environments (GitHub Actions runners, build containers) to non-whitelisted external hosts. Baseline legitimate build dependencies (npm CDN, PyPI mirrors, etc.) and alert on connections to dynamic DNS, newly-registered domains, or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate with process ancestry (npm/pip parent processes making network calls).

suggestion.title: Secrets Exfiltration via Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks steal GitHub tokens, npm auth tokens, database credentials, and API keys. Article title implies multiple attack vectors across 48 hours — all likely target credential theft. Pipeline did not detect environment variable access, .env file reads, or secret manager queries during package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package install processes (npm, pip, gem executables) for access to sensitive files (.env, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, credentials.json) or environment variable enumeration. Alert if post-install hooks or top-level install scripts execute shell commands that access or exfiltrate secrets (e.g., `cat $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa | curl ...`). Baseline legitimate install-time env var reads and flag novel patterns.

suggestion.title: Windows Server Service RPC Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'crafted RPC request that triggers an overflow during path canonicalization'—this is the direct attack mechanism and technical signature for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor RPC traffic to Windows Server Service (port 445/135) for payloads with abnormal size distributions, repeated connection failures, or path canonicalization sequences containing excessive backslash/dot patterns. Correlate with svchost.exe crashes or Event ID 7034 (service crashed unexpectedly).

suggestion.title: svchost.exe Server Service Crash Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow vulnerability inherently causes process termination; article describes the vulnerability as triggering 'overflow during path canonicalization' which would crash the hosting svchost process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected crashes or rapid sequential restarts of svchost.exe hosting the LanmanServer service. Establish baseline crash frequency and flag deviations; pair with RPC connection logs to distinguish exploitation from legitimate failures.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2008-4250 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal patch deadline 2026-06-03; requires continuous patch compliance scanning as preventive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch management systems for Windows systems lacking KB or security patch for CVE-2008-4250. Alert on any unpatched systems in production with network exposure and prior to federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: RPC Path Traversal Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is triggered 'during path canonicalization'—malformed path sequences in RPC Server Service calls are the direct exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect RPC requests to Server Service for path canonicalization abuse (excessive dot-dot-slash sequences, mixed separators, UNC path abuse, or canonicalization handler errors). Flag calls requesting file operations with malformed paths.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Inbound RPC Traffic Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attackers'—exploitation would manifest as elevated RPC connection attempts from external/untrusted networks to the vulnerable Server Service port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal inbound RPC connection rate to port 445/135 from non-whitelisted external subnets or geographic regions. Correlate with Windows Server Service error logs (Event ID 7001, 7000) and process crash events to confirm exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2009-1537 Vulnerable DirectX/DirectShow Components
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Microsoft DirectX contains a NULL byte overwrite vulnerability in the QuickTime Movie Parser Filter in quartz.dll in DirectShow'—this is the exploitation target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected loading of quartz.dll, dxva2.dll, or d3d9.dll in non-media processes. Flag process execution combining DirectShow component load with subsequent .mov/.qt file handling. Alert on DirectShow-related crash events with memory access violation codes (0xC0000005).

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted QuickTime Media File Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted QuickTime media file'—file delivery and player invocation is the initial compromise chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .mov, .qt, .quicktime files delivered via email attachment or downloaded from non-video-hosting sources. Correlate with user execution of media playback (wmplayer.exe, explorer.exe, media player) within 60 seconds of file receipt or download.

suggestion.title: CVE-2009-1537 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Scan Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates: 'CVE-2009-1537—match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-03'—inventory and compliance scanning is the detection baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2009-1537 matches. Flag any unpatched DirectX installations as critical risk ahead of 2026-06-03 federal deadline. Cross-reference asset inventory with patch records to identify patch lag.

suggestion.title: DirectShow Process Anomalous Behavior and Crash Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'NULL byte overwrite vulnerability'—buffer overflows generate distinctive exception and crash signatures detectable in process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DirectShow-invoking processes (explorer.exe, wmplayer.exe, dxdiag.exe) crashing with memory access violations following .mov/.qt file interaction. Flag unexpected child process spawning from media player context as heap spray or code-execution indicator.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Media File Origin and Handling Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attackers' implying network-based delivery; correlating file origin, file type, and player invocation strengthens exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .mov/.qt files from external email domains, non-video-hosting web sources, or with obfuscated filenames (double extensions, Unicode tricks). Escalate if followed by DirectShow process execution within short time window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2009-3459 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL.' CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation. Federal remediation deadline 2026-06-03 establishes urgency. Vulnerability scanner + asset inventory query is the canonical SOC response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners for Acrobat Reader versions matching vulnerable ranges for CVE-2009-3459. Flag unpatched instances on internet-facing systems and federal civilian agency networks. Cross-reference against patch-deployment logs to detect patch lag.

suggestion.title: PDF Exploit Delivery via Email / Web
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack vector is 'crafted PDF file.' Email gateways and web proxies should surface delivery of suspicious PDFs with heap-corruption triggers. No specific delivery mechanism given, but PDF is primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PDF files with anomalous structure (malformed headers, embedded executable objects, unusual entropy) arriving via email or web download. Correlate with subsequent Acrobat/Reader process crashes or anomalous behavior to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from Acrobat/Reader
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability outcome: 'execute arbitrary code via a crafted PDF.' Heap-overflow-to-RCE typically manifests as unexpected child processes spawned from AcroRd32.exe or acrobat.exe (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, rundll32.exe).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child process spawned from Acrobat or Reader process, especially interpreters (cmd, powershell) or system tools (rundll32, certutil). Low false-positive if filtered against whitelisted plugins. High-fidelity RCE indicator.

suggestion.title: Acrobat/Reader Process Crash or Fault Detection
suggestion.rationale: Heap-based buffer overflow typically manifests as process crash or access-violation fault before successful code execution. Early detection of abnormal Acrobat/Reader termination may catch exploitation in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Acrobat or Reader process crashes (exit codes 0xC0000374 heap-corruption, 0xC0000005 access violation, others). Correlate with recent PDF file access. Can be noisy but valuable as early-warning signal in high-risk environments.

suggestion.title: Unpatched IE Detection on Public-Facing Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [template]'. Need to detect public-facing IE systems not remediated by federal due date 2026-06-03.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match CVE-2010-0806 from vulnerability scanner output against systems with exposed RDP/HTTP ports and IE process registration. Alert on gap between scan date and federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: IE Patch Compliance by Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-03' as compliance obligation. Pipeline should track remediation status and flag non-compliance before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management logs for CVE-2010-0806 remediation dates; identify systems still vulnerable as of 2026-06-02; flag for urgent escalation given federal mandate.

suggestion.title: IE Process Execution on Public-Facing Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'currently being exploited' (CISA KEV criterion) and vectors involve 'access to an invalid pointer.' Need behavioral detection of suspicious IE execution or crash patterns on internet-facing assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on iexplore.exe or ieexec.exe process execution on assets with open ports 80/443; add memory exception/crash signals; correlate with access logs from non-routine sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-41091 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-41091 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and establishes federal patch deadline 2026-06-03. No detection use case generated despite clear scanning requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Microsoft Defender installations missing patch for CVE-2026-41091. Cross-reference asset inventory against known-vulnerable versions. Prioritize scan results with high exposure (internet-facing or directly internet-accessible systems). Alert on missing security updates targeting this CVE with 2026-06-03 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Privilege Escalation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'elevate privileges locally' via link-following vulnerability. This privilege escalation behavior should be hunted post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Microsoft Defender process (DefenderUI.exe, MpCmdRun.exe, NisSrv.exe) for suspicious privilege elevation attempts immediately following link/URL interaction. Alert on token elevation, privilege token creation, or unexpected administrator-context process spawning from Defender's process tree.

suggestion.title: Defender Link/URL Interaction Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'link following vulnerability' in Microsoft Defender. This specific interaction pattern should be detectable in Defender logs or process execution events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious URL or link processing within Microsoft Defender process context. Look for Defender spawning child processes with unusual command-line parameters, network connections to unexpected domains, or file access patterns triggered by link/URL parsing. Correlate with known exploit delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Authorized User Defender Privilege Escalation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authorized attacker' can exploit, narrowing attack surface to authenticated sessions. Detection should focus on privilege escalation post-authentication within user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authenticated users performing privilege escalation immediately after interacting with Defender (link clicks, URL processing, settings modifications). Alert on UAC bypass attempts, token theft, or unexpected elevation from normal user context to SYSTEM/admin.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Scan for CVE-2026-41091 — Federal Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes federal patch due-date 2026-06-03. Organizations must demonstrate patch compliance or mitigation by deadline. Compliance tracking is essential SOC function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory weekly through 2026-06-03 for Microsoft Defender version and patch status for CVE-2026-41091. Generate compliance reports grouped by exposure level (internet-facing, DMZ, internal). Alert on systems remaining vulnerable after 2026-05-27 (1 week before deadline) with escalating severity as deadline approaches.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45498 Patch Compliance Against Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-03' and states 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Pipeline failed to extract this deadline or propose compliance tracking detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Microsoft Defender patch version against CVE-2026-45498 remediation timeline. Alert on unpatched or non-compliant systems, especially those past 2026-06-03 deadline. Correlate scanner outputs with patching workflow status to identify remediation lag.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Service Disruption and Repeated Crash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'allows for denial of service' against Defender itself—a direct impact indicator. Pipeline missed this impact-phase detection despite 'denial of service' being the explicit attack type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal Microsoft Defender process termination, repeated service crashes, or restart cycles within short time windows. Correlate with Defender health telemetry (service unavailability events). Baseline normal restart frequency and alert on anomalous patterns coinciding with exploitation timeframes.

suggestion.title: Exposed Microsoft Defender Asset Hunt for Active Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets).' Pipeline failed to suggest this asset-discovery use case despite being core to CISA KEV methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems with Microsoft Defender services or APIs reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner inventory for CVE-2026-45498 presence. Flag systems in public-IP ranges running vulnerable versions; prioritize based on exposure and time-to-deadline.

suggestion.title: ExifTool Child Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'compromise Macs via single malicious image'—exploitation of ExifTool vulnerability via image parsing must spawn shell/code execution. Pipeline missed execution-phase indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ExifTool process (exiftool, perl) spawning unexpected child processes (bash, sh, zsh, python, curl, etc.). ExifTool normally reads metadata in-process; shell spawning indicates payload execution or command injection via malicious EXIF tags.

suggestion.title: Malicious Image File Delivery and Handling
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'single malicious image'—this is initial access vector. Pipeline failed to surface phishing-attachment or user-execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect image files (jpg, png, gif, exif-bearing formats) received from external email, messaging, or web downloads that are subsequently processed by image viewers, photo libraries, or ExifTool. Correlate file creation with executable spawning within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: ExifTool Version and Vulnerability Status
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability requires tracking patched vs. vulnerable ExifTool installations on macOS endpoints. Pipeline extracted no CVE identifier or software inventory indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory ExifTool presence and version on macOS endpoints (via 'exiftool -ver', package managers, brew list). Alert on pre-patch versions processing untrusted image files or when ExifTool version cannot be determined (suggesting older unmanaged installations).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Command-Line Arguments to ExifTool
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting image parsing vulnerability likely requires non-standard ExifTool invocation (e.g., tag injection, embedded shell syntax). Pipeline missed execution-mode analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ExifTool invocations with suspicious arguments: tag injection syntax (-tag=value with shell metacharacters), redirection (> >> |), backticks, $() subshells, or -execute directives. Baseline normal metadata-read workflows and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Reverse-Shell or C2 Communication Post-Image Processing
suggestion.rationale: Compromised macOS hosts via image exploit should beacon or attempt lateral movement. Article promises 'compromise'—pipeline missed impact/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ExifTool process execution or unexpected child processes with outbound network connections to non-standard ports, dynamic DNS, or known C2 infrastructure within 60 seconds. Include TLS handshake anomalies and suspicious DNS queries.

suggestion.title: Android Device Admin Activation for Kiosk Mode Lock
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'uses Kiosk Mode to Trap Victims'—this requires device admin privilege escalation. No detection use case proposed despite this being the core attack enabler and prerequisite for victim entrapment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device admin activation by third-party applications combined with Settings.Secure modifications that lock device to single app (kiosk mode). Flag rapid activation sequences or apps requesting admin privileges immediately after installation. Correlate with disable of home, back, and recents buttons.

suggestion.title: NFC Relay Attack Anomalies and Unexpected Transaction Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article's core attack vector is 'NFC Relay Attacks'—malware orchestrates abnormal NFC transactions toward attacker-controlled relay infrastructure. Pipeline failed to map this to T1623 or propose transaction-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual NFC transaction frequency, incomplete/failed transactions preceding successful ones, or transactions to unrecognized merchants. Flag transactions deviating from user baseline (amount, merchant, geography). Correlate with device-admin activation and kiosk-mode activation events within same session.

suggestion.title: Kiosk Mode Lockout Detection - User Unable to Exit Application
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes malware 'traps victims' via kiosk mode—user loses control and cannot escape. This user-facing impact is the direct indicator of successful attack, yet no detection case covers behavioral lockout patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Settings.Secure flags that disable home button, back button, recent-apps access, and status-bar visibility. Alert on accessibility service abuse that simulates kiosk constraints. Correlate with user support tickets reporting device lock-in incidents on same device/timestamp.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Installation and Package Sideloading
suggestion.rationale: DevilNFC as Android malware requires installation pathway (sideloaded APK, trojanized app, or phishing link). Article does not detail installation vector, but pipeline should have proposed detection for malware package installation regardless.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installation of APK files from non-Play-Store sources with device-admin permission requests. Monitor for package installation followed immediately (within 10s) by admin privilege grant. Alert on known malware package names (e.g., com.devilnfc.* if naming pattern known) or suspicious package signatures.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Fraud During Device Kiosk Lockout
suggestion.rationale: Article's impact is victim trapping during NFC attacks—attacker executes unauthorized financial transactions while victim cannot interact with device. No detection case mapped to T1634 (card fraud) or transaction anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device-kiosk-active events with financial transactions. Alert on transactions during periods when device is locked to single app. Flag rapid micro-transactions (credential testing) or transactions to new beneficiaries while kiosk is active. Monitor for suppressed transaction confirmations or disabled notifications.

suggestion.title: NFC Relay Hardware and Attacker Infrastructure Indicators
suggestion.rationale: NFC relay attacks require attacker-controlled hardware or relay devices positioned near victims. Pipeline should have proposed IOC detection for relay C2 infrastructure, Bluetooth/NFC pairing anomalies, or geospatial clustering of attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected Bluetooth or NFC device pairings, especially in retail/payment environments. Alert on devices making NFC transactions while in close proximity to multiple other NFC-relay-enabled devices (indicating relay attack cluster). Flag C2 communication to infrastructure associated with NFC relay attack tooling.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Public-Facing Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'FreePBX Vulnerability Allow Attackers to Gain Access to User Portals'—indicates exploitation of CVE against publicly exposed FreePBX instance. No detection logic was generated despite clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to FreePBX default paths (/admin, /config.php, /user_portal) with unusual user agents, payloads, or parameter fuzzing patterns. Correlate with failed authentication logs and subsequent successful access from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FreePBX User Portal Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Gain Access to User Portals'—suggests authentication bypass or privilege escalation post-exploitation. Pipeline failed to generate detection for unauthenticated or anomalous portal access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to FreePBX user portals immediately following failed authentication attempts from same source, or from IPs without prior FreePBX history. Baseline normal admin/user login patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Version Enumeration and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable FreePBX versions before exploitation. Title does not specify version constraints, but enterprise detection should cover reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to /admin/config.php?display=about, HTTP banner grabbing, or version-specific path probing against FreePBX instances. Look for scripted requests with low think-time and multiple consecutive requests to version-discovery endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FreePBX Shell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Once portal access is gained, attackers typically execute system commands via FreePBX administrative functions. Title does not detail post-compromise behavior; detection use case is critical for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution spawned from FreePBX application context (asterisk daemon, web server process running FreePBX code) with suspicious parent-child relationships or command-line arguments like shell invocations, reverse shells, or file transfers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious FreePBX Configuration Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers modify FreePBX configs for persistence (adding SIP peers, call forwarding, IVR manipulation). Title establishes 'Gain Access' but not persistence mechanisms; critical for persistence and impact phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to /etc/asterisk/, /opt/freepbx/, or FreePBX database config tables. Establish baseline of normal admin modification patterns and alert on after-hours changes, bulk modifications, or changes from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious @cap-js npm package installation by version
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'compromised versions of @cap-js/sqlite@2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres@2.2.2, and @cap-js/db-service@2.10.1 were published' on April 29, 2026. Direct installation detection vector via package manager audit logs and lock file analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn install, or pnpm install commands and package lock files for @cap-js packages at specified versions. Alert on installations within 14 days of April 29, 2026 compromise date to identify unpatched environments.

suggestion.title: Node.js process reading credential files and environment variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious packages harvested credentials' including 'npm tokens, cloud provider credentials, SSH keys, GitHub PATs'. Process file access to ~/.ssh, ~/.npm, ~/.aws, and sensitive environment variable reads are direct indicators of credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js or npm processes reading credential files (.ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .npmrc) or accessing sensitive environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY). High confidence if access originates from node_modules context.

suggestion.title: Malware self-propagation via npm publish or package manifest modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'attempted self-propagation' — indicates re-publishing to npm registry, package.json dependency injection, or lock file tampering. Detect npm publish commands and manifest edits by dev processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm publish commands from non-CI processes, unexpected package.json additions post-install, or suspicious package-lock.json modifications. Correlate with credential access events to establish compromise chain.

suggestion.title: C2 callback to zero.masscan.cloud or 94.154.172.43
suggestion.rationale: Article IOC section lists 'Domain (defanged): zero.masscan.cloud' and 'IPv4 (defanged): 94.154.172.43' as C2 infrastructure. Article itself provides working UC (UC_14_4) but pipeline extracted zero network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network connections from Node.js/npm processes to zero.masscan.cloud or 94.154.172.43. Track exfiltration patterns post-credential-access via DNS TXT records or HTTPS POST requests.

suggestion.title: File hash detection for @cap-js stealer payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article provides three SHA256 hashes in IOC section: 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34, 6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95, eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb. Pipeline extracted zero file hashes despite working UC (UC_14_5) in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for file operations, process executions, and DLL loads matching the three provided SHA256 hashes. Conduct 90-day retrohunt to identify complete scope of affected systems and historical compromise window (April 29 - May 20, 2026).

suggestion.title: Employee Device Compromise via Network Access to Internal Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Employee Device Hack' in title as initial access vector. This is the entry point to the kill chain and should trigger detection on anomalous device authentication patterns and network access from that device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee device(s) authenticating to internal GitHub infrastructure from new locations or after offline period. Correlate with timing of article claim (May 2026) against historical baseline of that device's network access patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) Creation and Usage
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of '~4,000 internal repositories' requires either stolen credentials or generated access tokens from compromised account. Article implies credential theft post-device-compromise. Detection should flag PAT creation from unfamiliar IPs and high-volume API calls to repository endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for PAT creation from non-standard locations, followed within hours by bulk repository enumeration (GET /repos, /user/repos) and content access (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents). Flag sequences of 50+ repo accesses from single token in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Clone/Download from Internal GitHub Instance
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies '3,800+ Internal Repos' exfiltrated. This volume of repository access and download is anomalous and detectable via GitHub API logs, bandwidth monitoring, or git clone patterns. Article establishes exfiltration as the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git clone operations targeting internal GitHub repos at scale (>10 clones/hour from single source). Also monitor for large outbound data transfers (GB scale) to external cloud storage or C2 infrastructure shortly after credential compromise.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Internal GitHub Lateral Movement and Repository Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Transition from employee device access to internal GitHub repository access implies lateral movement within GitHub's internal network/systems. Article says 'Internal Repositories' accessed, implying attacker moved from device to GitHub systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid repository enumeration (list operations on /repos, /user/repos endpoints) from newly-authenticated session or IP. Flag patterns of 100+ API calls querying repository metadata before cloning. Correlate with device login anomalies.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to External Cloud Storage or Dead-Drop Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 3,800+ repos implies transfer to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Article does not detail exfil destination, but typical patterns include S3 buckets, Google Drive, or attacker C2. Should detect egress to known malicious infrastructure or suspicious cloud storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted tunnels or HTTP(S) transfers to non-GitHub domains from compromised device or GitHub infrastructure. Alert on uploads to public cloud storage (s3.amazonaws.com, storage.googleapis.com, blob.core.windows.net) from internal GitHub systems. Flag DNS queries for known TeamPCP C2 domains or dead-drop infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Execution in GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When the malicious npm package was released, Grafana's CI/CD workflow consumed it, and the info-stealer module executed in its GitHub environment.' This is initial compromise—dependency execution in CI/CD must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for npm install followed by suspicious child process spawning (curl, env, printenv, python -c). Cross-reference installed versions against known-malicious package hashes from threat intel feeds (Socket.dev, JFrog, Phylum). Alert on unsigned code execution in workflows.

suggestion.title: GitHub Workflow Token Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the info-stealer module executed in its GitHub environment, exfiltrating GitHub workflow tokens to the attackers.' Detect credential harvesting from CI/CD environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution of environment variable dumpers (env, printenv, set) within GitHub Actions. Monitor for outbound HTTP/DNS from CI runners to unknown/newly-registered domains. Alert on GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable access by non-GitHub processes.

suggestion.title: Repository Access and Cloning Using Compromised Workflow Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the attacker used it to gain access to the company's private repositories' and 'the attacker obtained a GitHub workflow token that provided access to Grafana's repositories.' Detect lateral movement via token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls using workflow tokens for unexpected repository clones or large data exports. Alert on git operations from non-standard geolocation or ASN. Cross-reference token creation date with incident discovery date (May 1) to identify missed-rotation tokens.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Source Code Download During Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the intruders stole source code' and 'the attacker downloaded operational information.' Monitor for bulk repository access and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple repository clones in rapid succession using a single token. Monitor for git archive/bundle operations or large pack file transfers. Correlate with outbound traffic to non-Grafana-controlled infrastructure (e.g., attacker-controlled S3, GitHub gists).

suggestion.title: Delayed or Incomplete Credential Rotation Post-Incident
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Grafana detected malicious activity on May 1...and immediately deployed the incident response plan, which included rotating GitHub workflow tokens. However, one token was missed in the process.' Detect gaps in incident response execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub workflow tokens created before May 1 that were NOT rotated in the May 1–May 2 window. Monitor for use of pre-incident tokens after rotation deadline. Alert if a token remains active >48h post-incident after similar tokens were rotated.

suggestion.title: Info-Stealer Callback to External C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration of tokens 'to the attackers' but does not specify C2 domain. The info-stealer module must callback to receive commands or exfil stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and HTTP/HTTPS traffic from GitHub Actions runners to external IPs. Flag newly registered domains (WHOIS age <7 days) queried from CI environments. Detect post-install script HTTP requests (curl/wget from npm scripts) to non-artifact domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation from Compromised Org
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates TanStack npm attack—pipeline should surface detection for installation of malicious versions from compromised namespace or publisher account
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/ci commands targeting TanStack packages; correlate with package version timeline around breach date; flag versions not matching official release signatures.

suggestion.title: GitHub PAT Exfiltration via npm Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm commonly harvest GitHub PATs from environment or .git/config during package install—article describes 'source code exposure' suggesting credential theft
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm post-install scripts accessing .git, .github, or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable; detect process spawning with credential-exfil patterns (curl/wget to external domains with token-like strings).

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from Grafana Build/CI Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Breach of Grafana GitHub suggests attacker gained CI/CD access—source code exposure implies exfiltration or C2 beaconing from build agents
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from CI/build nodes (GitHub Actions runners, Grafana CI infrastructure) to unfamiliar domains post-incident; flag DNS queries or HTTP POST to domains registered post-breach date.

suggestion.title: SonicWall CVE-2024-12802 MFA Bypass via UPN Login Format
suggestion.rationale: "Missing MFA enforcement for the UPN login format, allowing an attacker with valid credentials to authenticate directly and bypass the MFA requirement." Core attack vector, Gen6 only.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events where Gen6 SonicWall device processes UPN-format login (userPrincipalName) without completing MFA challenge. Alert on successful VPN access where LDAP auth succeeded but MFA response code missing or null. Verify SonicWall configuration lacks 'Qualified login name' constraint.

suggestion.title: Scripted/Automated VPN Access via sess="CLI" Parameter
suggestion.rationale: "The sess=\"CLI\" signal is a key indicator of these attacks, which suggests scripted or automated VPN authentication." Specific log signature provided by ReliaQuest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any VPN authentication log entry containing sess="CLI" parameter. Filter out legitimate administrative API calls. Correlate with multiple login attempts in 30-minute window and credential reuse across accounts to identify brute-force + MFA bypass pattern.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Authentication Event ID 238/1080 Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: "Other strong signals are event IDs 238 and 1080, and VPN logins from suspicious VPS/VPN infrastructure." ReliaQuest identified as reliable indicators of CVE-2024-12802 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SonicWall logs for Event IDs 238 and 1080 appearing without corresponding MFA completion markers. Alert on sequences of these events followed by successful internal access within 30-60 minutes. Cross-reference with failed/retried login attempts.

suggestion.title: RDP Lateral Movement from VPN Session with Local Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: "Hacker gained access to the internal network and reached a domain-joined file server... established a remote connection over RDP using a shared local administrator password." Classic post-exploitation lateral move.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP logon (Event 4624, Logon Type 10) to file servers within 30 minutes of VPN authentication. Alert when RDP actor is local admin account and source is internal VPN IP. Escalate if same session shows failed RDP attempts before success (credential testing).

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Process Execution and C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: "The attacker tried to deploy a Cobalt Strike beacon, a post-exploitation framework for command-and-control (C2) communication." Execution phase, attempted despite EDR block.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cobalt Strike beacon signatures: rundll32/powershell process spawning with suspicious injection patterns, HTTP POST beaconing to non-standard ports, memory injection via CreateRemoteThread. Monitor for DNS queries to Cobalt Strike default C2 domains and JA3/TLS fingerprint anomalies.

suggestion.title: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) Loading Attempt
suggestion.rationale: "Tried to deploy... a vulnerable driver, likely to disable endpoint protection using the Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) technique." Defense evasion mechanism targeting EDR, ultimately blocked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned/revoked driver load attempts from user-writable directories (AppData, Temp, Downloads). Flag known-vulnerable driver names (gdrv.sys, DBUtil_2_3.sys, GIGABYTE, MSI variants). Correlate with recent EDR process termination or anomaly in Sysmon Event ID 6 (driver load).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Tax-Themed Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake income tax assessment pages'—initial access vector. Should detect access to newly registered or spoofed domains impersonating tax authorities (malformed *.tax TLDs, non-official tax.gov lookalikes, tax keywords on suspicious registrars).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users resolving/connecting to domains with 'tax', 'irs', 'assessment' keywords registered <30 days ago, or non-government ASNs claiming to be .gov domains. Alert on redirect chains from legitimate-looking tax pages to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Fake Tax Page Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'infect Windows systems'—execution phase. Detect suspicious process execution immediately after downloads from non-official tax domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file downloads (from non-tax-authority domains) to %Downloads% or %temp%, then alert on child process execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, .exe/.scr/.zip launch) within 2 minutes. Flag if parent process is browser.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Registration—Tax Authority Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires registering fake tax assessment domains. Should detect newly registered domains mimicking tax infrastructure: 'fake income tax assessment pages' indicates domain registration with spoofing intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WHOIS registrations with tax keywords in last 30 days, non-government registrars, or nameservers outside official tax authority IP ranges. Cross-reference against historical .gov CNAME records to catch lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Domain Masquerading—Legitimate Tax Authority Brand Abuse
suggestion.rationale: 'Fake income tax assessment pages' is a masquerading attack. Should detect domains or pages using legitimate tax authority visual/textual identity without legitimate source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSL certificates issued for domains containing 'tax', 'irs', 'revenue' but registered to non-government entities. Alert on HTTPS connections where cert CN/SAN claims government authority but issuer is third-party CA or self-signed.

suggestion.title: FsTx Malicious File Placement on USB or EFI Partition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'placing specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive or EFI partition, rebooting into WinRE.' This is the primary attack delivery vector; pipeline extracted no file-based IOCs or detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or presence of files with FsTx extension on USB-connected devices, external media, or EFI system partitions. Alert on any FsTx file activity as they are non-standard Windows components. Correlate with subsequent WinRE boot or shell spawning events.

suggestion.title: WinRE Shell Execution via CTRL Key Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'triggering a shell with unrestricted access to the BitLocker-protected storage volume by holding down the CTRL key.' Pipeline completely missed this execution and privilege-escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from WinRE or Recovery Partition context with file system access spanning BitLocker volumes. Flag abnormal parent processes during boot recovery scenarios. Monitor for CTRL key sequences during WinRE if telemetry available.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification: BootExecute autofstx.exe Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation: 'removing the autofstx.exe entry from the Session Manager's BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ value.' Attackers may preemptively remove this defense; registry modification was not extracted as IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager BootExecute value for removal or disabling of autofstx.exe entries. Alert on any modification to BootExecute REG_MULTI_SZ. Baseline legitimate entries and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BitLocker Configuration Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Article advises configuring BitLocker from 'TPM-only' to 'TPM+PIN' mode as mitigation. Attackers may reverse this; pipeline missed detection for BitLocker security posture degradation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BitLocker configuration transitions from TPM+PIN back to TPM-only or suspension of pre-boot authentication. Alert on unexpected BitLocker disablement or key material export. Track administrative BitLocker cmdlet execution (Disable-BitLocker, Suspend-BitLocker).

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Definition Update Blocking (UnDefend Zero-Day)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'UnDefend, another zero-day that attackers with standard user permissions can exploit to block Microsoft Defender definition updates.' Defense-evasion technique with standard-user exploitation—no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Defender definition update failures, service disruptions, and signature push failures. Alert on repeated failed update attempts followed by Defender degradation. Correlate timing with suspicious non-admin process execution.

suggestion.title: Active Exploitation of BlueHammer / GreenPlasma LPE Zero-Days
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) and RedSun...are now being exploited in attacks' and 'GreenPlasma...attackers can abuse to obtain a SYSTEM shell.' Both active exploits with zero IOCs extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation from user context to SYSTEM without explicit elevation prompts, consistent with LPE exploitation. Track suspicious code paths known to trigger BlueHammer, GreenPlasma, or RedSun. Alert on abnormal process nesting and token elevation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Code-Signed Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'malware-signing service behind ransomware attacks' — suggests threat actors obtaining valid code signatures to bypass Windows SmartScreen and UAC warnings. Missing UC for detecting execution of binaries with suspicious signing certificates or recently-issued certs tied to known malicious services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with code signatures issued by newly-discovered CAs, or signatures failing chain-of-trust validation. Alert on binaries signed by certificates subsequently revoked by Microsoft. Cross-reference signer thumbprints against blacklists of known malware-signing services.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Signed Package
suggestion.rationale: Article implies ransomware delivery mechanism using valid signatures. Missing UC for detecting suspicious download/execution patterns of newly-signed executables, especially those distributed through common infection vectors (email, watering holes, supply chain).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of executables with code signatures issued within 7 days of known ransomware families. Flag cases where download source is unusual for software distribution (personal email, file-sharing services). Correlate with ransomware telemetry.

suggestion.title: Certificate Authority Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Service that signs malware implies either CA compromise or insider abuse of legitimate certificate-issuing authority. Missing UC for detecting anomalous certificate issuance patterns, bulk signing requests, or creation of intermediate CAs by unauthorized accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor certificate request/issuance logs for unusual patterns: batch requests, out-of-hours signing, issuance to non-whitelisted departments, or requests by newly-created service accounts. Alert on creation of subordinate CAs or changes to certificate validation policies.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Installation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title states extension was 'Compromised'—implies malicious install/update. Pipeline missed detection for unexpected extension installs across organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console VS Code extension installations where the extension was not previously present in the environment. Alert on version downgrades or installs from non-standard sources. Baseline approved extension versions and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Build Process Behavioral Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension would alter Nx CLI behavior. Phrase 'Compromised' implies runtime malicious activity during build execution. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of anomalous child processes or network egress during builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected child processes spawned by Nx CLI (npm, node, build tools). Alert when unexpected processes (PowerShell, cmd, curl, wget) execute during Nx build phase. Detect exfiltration-pattern network connections (DNS, HTTPS to non-CDN domains) initiated from Nx CLI context.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Manifest Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of extension implies malicious manifest modification or unauthorized code injection. Pipeline missed detection for extension metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to extension manifest files (package.json, extension metadata in %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions). Alert on unsigned or untrusted manifest updates. Detect injection of new entry points or script changes post-installation.

suggestion.title: Build Pipeline Credential Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev tool could steal build-time credentials (git tokens, npm tokens, cloud keys). Title alone establishes high-privilege execution context. Pipeline failed to suggest monitoring for credential exfiltration during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution reading credential files (.npmrc, .git/config, ssh keys, environment variables) during Nx build execution. Detect environment-variable enumeration (env, printenv) or credential-store queries. Alert on exfiltration of these values over HTTP/HTTPS to non-organization domains.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Version Control Integrity
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension implies version pinning bypass or malicious auto-update. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of unexpected extension version transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Nx Console extension version across all developer machines. Alert on spontaneous version changes (especially downgrades or jumps to unsigned/beta versions). Detect registry/manifest modifications that disable extension signature verification or allow unsigned extensions.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Nx CLI Execution Profile Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise means malicious code executes in every developer's build context. Pipeline failed to suggest baseline detection for abnormal Nx invocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Nx CLI command-line patterns, invocation frequency, and timing across developer population. Alert on statistical outliers: unusual times of day, abnormal command-line arguments, invocations from user accounts not typically running builds. Detect lateral spread patterns (same compromise signals across multiple machines in short time window).

suggestion.title: Setuid/Setgid Binary Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Local Privilege Escalation Flaw Allows Silent Root Access' — Pardus Linux CVEs typically exploit setuid/setgid mechanisms. Detection needed for suspicious setuid bit modifications or execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected changes to setuid/setgid bits on system binaries, execution of setuid-enabled binaries from anomalous directories, or parent-child relationships violating expected privilege inheritance. Baseline per-user capability sets.

suggestion.title: Sudo Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Local Privilege Escalation Flaw' — common Linux vector involves sudo misconfiguration or CVE. Sudo execution patterns must be monitored for exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocation with NOPASSWD flag, sudo execution by non-standard users, unusual command-line arguments, or sudo commands executing scripts from world-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Unexpected UID 0 Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Allows Silent Root Access' — must detect privilege escalation from unprivileged user to UID 0. Baseline user privilege levels and detect unauthorized transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline UID/GID per user and process. Alert on unexpected privilege level transitions (unprivileged → UID 0, or unprivileged → system groups). Monitor process ancestry for privilege boundary violations.

suggestion.title: Kernel Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Pardus Linux privilege escalation CVEs frequently exploit kernel vulnerabilities. Title 'Flaw Allows Silent Root Access' suggests kernel-level attack vector. Detection must monitor for kernel-level anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious syscall patterns associated with kernel exploits (ptrace/ioctl sequences, direct memory access, mmap with unusual flags), kernel module loading from user processes, or abnormal exception/segfault clustering.

suggestion.title: Pardus Linux System Binary Integrity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation CVEs exploit vulnerabilities in core system utilities. Pardus-specific binaries likely to be targets. Detection requires file integrity baseline against package manifest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hash and permission integrity of privilege-escalation-sensitive binaries (/usr/bin/sudo, /bin/mount, /usr/sbin/useradd, /bin/ls, /bin/chmod). Alert on modification timestamp anomalies or permission changes outside patch windows.

suggestion.title: Linux Privilege Escalation via PinTheft Exploit Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states vulnerability 'Let Attackers Gain Root Access' on Linux. Detection should identify exploitation attempts and successful privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Linux privilege escalation syscalls (setuid, setgid, CAP_SYS_ADMIN usage) correlating with PinTheft exploit signatures. Alert on unexpected transitions from non-root to root context, particularly via exploitation vectors. Baseline normal privilege escalation patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Public PinTheft PoC Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'PoC Released', signaling public availability of working exploit. Early detection of PoC usage prevents exploitation cascades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track download and execution of PinTheft public exploits. Monitor for characteristic PoC filenames, repository URLs (GitHub, GitLab), or signature patterns. Alert when users execute unknown binaries or scripts targeting Linux privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Access Patterns on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Root access is the stated impact. Should detect unauthorized elevation outside expected maintenance windows or change control processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authorized root access initiators (sudo users, service accounts) and elevation timing. Alert on root shell spawns from unexpected parent processes, out-of-window escalations, or repeated failed privilege escalation attempts indicating exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable System Identification - PinTheft Linux Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Linux-specific vulnerability requires asset discovery. Title constrains scope to Linux platform; pipeline should drive inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Linux systems. Cross-reference against PinTheft CVE data (when disclosed) to identify vulnerable Linux kernel versions, distributions, or configurations. Flag unpatched systems and track remediation timelines.

suggestion.title: Gaming Account Credential Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata states goal of 'securing gaming communities' (from description)—credential attacks are the primary initial-access vector for gaming account compromise. Pipeline should have inferred this from title/description despite corrupted body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect brute-force and spray attacks targeting gaming accounts: >10 failed logins per account within 5 minutes, >50 failed logins across unique accounts in 10 minutes, or MFA exhaustion attempts. Correlate with IP reputation, geolocation anomalies, and user-profile baseline.

suggestion.title: Gaming Account Takeover via Session Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Metadata references 'unique challenges' of securing gaming platforms—session hijacking and account takeover are core threats requiring detection based on deviation from baseline player behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-account baselines (login time-of-day, geography, device type, in-game activity cadence). Alert on suspicious deviations: login from new country without prior access, impossible travel >1000km/h between sessions, or in-game activity at times inconsistent with historical player pattern.

suggestion.title: Gaming Service Availability Attack (DDoS)
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Securing the gaming' and emphasis on protecting platforms implies availability is a core concern. Gaming platforms are high-value DDoS targets; this UC should have been generated from title context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric and application-layer DDoS: sustained traffic >3x baseline during off-peak hours, abnormal packet-per-second variance, HTTP requests with low user-agent diversity, or rapid connection-exhaustion patterns. Correlate with player-latency spikes and session-drop rates.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Process Accessing Credential Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes credential theft as attack outcome: 'poisoned extension breached GitHub' implies unauthorized access to GitHub credentials, likely via extension code reading .git config or environment variables containing PAT tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension host process (codeserver.exe, extension.js runner) for file system access to .git/config, .gitconfig, or .ssh directories. Alert on reads of GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN environment variables or access to credential manager APIs from extension context.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'poisoned extension' indicates the extension itself is the attack vector; either installed maliciously or compromised after legitimate installation. Pipeline should detect unusual extension installation sources or unsigned extension loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension installation from non-official registry (typosquatted package name in extensions.json, offline .vsix install, or HTTP-only download). Monitor for extensions requesting file system or network permissions. Track extension installation sources and flag registry writes from non-VSCode processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Activity from VS Code Extension Host
suggestion.rationale: Breaching GitHub implies exfiltration of credentials to attacker infrastructure; extension code must beacon out to C2 domain with stolen tokens. Title establishes external data flow: 'poisoned extension...breached GitHub' = data egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound domains from VS Code extension host process (code-server, vscode-server). Alert on: DNS queries to suspicious TLDs, HTTPS connections to rare/never-seen domains from extension context, POST requests with base64 or URL-encoded credential-like data patterns, or connections to known malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via VS Code Extension Load
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: extension runs arbitrary JavaScript in privileged VS Code context. Title 'poisoned extension' implies code execution as primary payload delivery. Pipeline should detect extension activation hooks loading arbitrary code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension activation events for suspicious entry points: extensions.json declaring non-standard activation events (on-demand, wildcard patterns), extension.js/index.js files containing eval(), require('child_process'), or obfuscated code. Alert on extensions modifying PATH or installing shell scripts during activation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Developer Machine to GitHub via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title outcome: 'breached GitHub' — implies attacker pivoted from compromised developer machine to GitHub account using stolen credentials. Pipeline should detect suspicious GitHub API calls or git push/clone operations from non-standard contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: git commands (push, clone, config) executed from VS Code extension process or child process. Monitor for unusual GitHub API calls (Create repos, list private repos, push to unexpected branches) using stolen PAT tokens. Correlate with extension code execution timeline and credential access events.

suggestion.title: Persistence via VS Code Extension Autostart
suggestion.rationale: For sustained breach, attacker extension must survive restarts and reinstalls. Title 'extension' implies it persists across sessions. Should detect extensions modifying VS Code settings, user data, or system startup mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or malicious extensions modifying settings.json (autoload, execute on startup), creating VS Code keybindings pointing to attacker payloads, or writing to %APPDATA%/Code/User/globalStorage for persistence markers. Alert on extensions registering shell commands or modifying system PATH.

suggestion.title: Certificate Subject Reuse Across Malware Families
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse'; indicates shared certificate infrastructure across multiple malware families (TamperedChef, DocuFlex, EvilAI). Pipeline must detect clustering via certificate fingerprint/subject commonality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events where unsigned or self-signed certificates match between samples attributed to different malware families. Correlate certificate subjects/issuers across DeviceProcessEvents and TLS traffic logs to identify infrastructure reuse patterns indicating coordinated campaigns.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign to RAT Delivery Chain
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'malvertising' and 'Remote Access Trojan'; article discusses trojanized productivity apps delivered via malicious ads. No detection for malvertising vector in output despite being primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious ad network redirects followed by executable downloads and process execution. Correlate malvertising infrastructure (ad domains) with known RAT C2 infrastructure; flag process execution chains initiated from browser with parent process being updater or productivity app.

suggestion.title: Code Similarity Clustering for TamperedChef Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Code Reuse' as clustering signal; indicates multiple samples share significant code portions. Pipeline should surface code similarity thresholds (fuzzy hash matches, TLSH) as attribution technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag binaries with high code similarity (TLSH ≥ 80, ssdeep ≥ 85) to known TamperedChef samples in event logs or endpoint telemetry. Track file hashes uploaded to internal sandbox or downloaded from external sources; correlate similarity scores with known campaign identifiers (CL-CRI-1089, CL-UNK-1090).

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies malware family as 'Remote Access Trojan'; RATs inherently perform C2 communication. Keywords field explicitly lists this attack type. No detection use case generated for RAT-specific C2 patterns despite high severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing patterns: regular outbound connections from known trojanized app processes to low-reputation domains; DNS queries for dynamic DNS providers; unusual port usage (non-standard HTTP/HTTPS). Correlate process ancestry (browser → updater → RAT process) with network events.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Productivity Application Launch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Metadata references 'Appsuite PDF' and trojanized productivity apps as delivery vehicle. No detection for modified/replaced legitimate applications despite this being primary infection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation from unexpected paths for legitimate applications (e.g., Adobe Reader, Microsoft Office not in Program Files); monitor for file replacement events in app directories; correlate with subsequent child process execution for unsigned or obfuscated binaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via RAT Persistence
suggestion.rationale: RAT capabilities inherently include credential harvesting. Article severity [CRIT] combined with 'Remote Access Trojan' classification indicates credential exfiltration is core objective. Pipeline missed RAT-specific credential access TTPs.
