suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git clone operations (≥10 repos within 10 minutes) from single source using identical PAT/session. Monitor for concurrent SSH key uploads or clone destinations to cloud storage buckets (S3, Blob).

suggestion.title: Installation of Unsigned or Typosquatted VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Core vector described in title: 'poisoned extension'—indicates installation from untrusted source, marketplace impersonation, or supply-chain trojanization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory for installations lacking valid Microsoft publisher signatures. Alert on extensions with names similar to legitimate tools (Jira, GitHub, Azure) or installs from non-official marketplace sources, including direct file drops to extensions folder.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Embedded schema.org description explicitly states 'malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads'; keywords include 'malvertising' as primary attack vector. No detection UC generated despite clear attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for advertising network domains flagged as malware distribution vectors. Alert on connections to ad tech infrastructure followed by executable downloads from non-standard ports. Correlate with known malvertising campaign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Productivity Application Detection
suggestion.rationale: Schema.org description embedded in page explicitly states 'trojanized productivity apps' as delivery method. This is a primary attack surface mentioned in article metadata but generated no UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on productivity application executables with hash mismatches against known-good versions. Monitor for unsigned or revoked signatures on legitimate application names. Detect file replacements in typical installation paths (Program Files, Applications).

suggestion.title: Certificate Reuse Pattern Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'via Certificate and Code Reuse' as malware clustering mechanism. This suggests certificate fingerprints are a key forensic indicator, but no certificate-based detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build fingerprint database of TLS certificates observed across TamperedChef malware samples and C2 infrastructure. Alert when previously-seen certificates appear on new infrastructure or new malware hashes, indicating related campaigns or infrastructure reuse.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Command-and-Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly identify 'Remote Access Trojan' and 'RATs' as attack payloads. No C2 communication detection UC generated despite RATs requiring persistent C&C traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent connections to DocuFlex and EvilAI malware family C2 domains. Detect beaconing patterns on non-standard ports. Track DNS lookups to infrastructure known to host TamperedChef command servers.

suggestion.title: Code Similarity Clustering for Malware Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Code Reuse' as a malware clustering mechanism. This indicates fuzzy code matching is a detection pillar, but no code-similarity UC was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply fuzzy hashing (SSDEEP, TLSH) to submitted binaries and alert on high-similarity matches with known TamperedChef variants. Use entropy analysis and static code section matching to identify reused code blocks, enabling variant detection.

suggestion.title: TamperedChef Malware Family Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords directly name threat actor 'TamperedChef,' malware families 'DocuFlex' and 'EvilAI,' and threat IDs 'CL-CRI-1089', 'CL-UNK-1090'. No family-specific detection rules generated despite explicit threat naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create YARA and signature-based alerts for known TamperedChef file hashes, behavioral indicators, and malware family markers (DocuFlex resource sections, EvilAI process injection patterns). Correlate execution with MITRE technique chains specific to this threat family.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mass Android App Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '455 Malicious Apps'—distributed ad fraud requires installing dozens or hundreds of apps per device. Pipeline missed detection for rapid app installation clustering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of app installations clustered within short time windows (e.g., >20 installs/hour). Baseline user app install patterns and alert on deviations exceeding 2–3σ. Flag side-loaded or third-party store installations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Ad Click Generation Without User Intent
suggestion.rationale: Core TTP from title: 'Generate Fake Clicks'—malware must programmatically trigger ad interactions at inhuman velocity. Pipeline did not surface detection for bot-like click behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for click events with sub-100ms inter-arrival times, zero concurrent motion sensor data (accelerometer, magnetometer), or click patterns misaligned with user touch events. Alert on click volume >10× median user baseline.

suggestion.title: Persistent Background Service Registration by Untrusted Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sustained ad fraud operation ('operation')—requires persistence. Apps must register background services or receivers to survive reboots and system updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps requesting android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED or registering JobScheduler/WorkManager tasks without user-facing UI. Monitor for high-frequency receiver/service registrations from newly installed apps.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Communication from Malicious Apps
suggestion.rationale: Operating 455 apps requires centralized coordination for payload delivery and targeting. Pipeline did not detect C2 communication patterns from app processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or IP connections from app processes to infrastructure matching C2 naming patterns (fast-flux, dynamic subdomains). Flag connections to bulletproof hosting ASNs or domains with short TTLs and high churn.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Delivery and Runtime Code Loading
suggestion.rationale: Ad fraud malware requires dynamic payload delivery post-installation. Article scale ('455 apps') implies sophisticated update and evasion mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps downloading DEX files, ZIP archives, or encrypted payloads post-installation. Detect reflection-based code invocation (ClassLoader.loadClass, Method.invoke). Flag TLS connections with certificate pinning bypasses or weak ciphers.

suggestion.title: Elevation of Privilege via Vulnerable Android Framework Services
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale ad fraud campaigns may exploit framework vulnerabilities to escalate privileges and run payloads as SYSTEM. No privilege-escalation detections surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for setuid/setgid syscalls from app UIDs, binder-based elevation requests (ServiceManager calls), or capability acquisition (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN). Cross-reference with known Android privesc CVEs.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'infostealer malware that secretly infected users' devices, collected login credentials and transmitted them to servers controlled by the attackers.' Pipeline generated zero detection for malware execution phase despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing browser credential stores (sqlite files in Chrome/Firefox profiles) and reading Local State registry hives from non-browser parent processes. Monitor for suspicious process chains spawning explorer.exe or rundll32.exe to enumerate browser profile directories. Alert on modifications to browser startup paths and persistence mechanisms (Run registry keys, scheduled tasks launching malware).

suggestion.title: Stolen Session Token Abuse and MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'session tokens that can be used to log in to the victim's account without needing credentials and, in some cases, bypass multi-factor authentication.' This direct credential-access technique was not mapped to any detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser cookie/session file exfiltration by monitoring non-browser processes reading cookie databases (Chrome/Cookies, Firefox places.sqlite) and Local State files. Pair token exfiltration with authentication anomalies: successful logins from new geolocations without interactive authentication, or sessions bypassing MFA challenge within minutes of credential theft. Flag accounts with session login followed immediately by high-risk actions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized E-Commerce Purchase Fraud Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states '5,800 accounts...used to make unauthorized purchases totaling about $721,000.' This clear fraud impact was not mapped to detection. Article describes targeting 'users of an online store in California'—a specific merchant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with immediate post-breach purchase anomalies: same-day login from new IP plus purchase within 2–4 hours; multiple accounts (>5) from single source IP making purchases within 24h; high-value purchases from accounts with no prior transaction history or deviating significantly from baseline (category, amount, geography). Aggregate across California online store customers for bulk-fraud detection.

suggestion.title: Telegram C2 and Exfiltration Channel Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credentials 'sold through specialized online resources and Telegram bots' but no specific bot identifiers or traffic patterns are extracted. Detection should cover Telegram as a malware exfiltration channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and TLS connections to Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org) from processes exhibiting infostealer behavioral indicators (accessing credential stores, reading browser profiles). Flag Telegram bot token registrations and message POSTs from suspicious processes. Alert on bulk message transmissions from single client IP to multiple bot endpoints, indicative of credential exfiltration automation.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Transaction Proceeds Laundering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'suspect engaged in cryptocurrency transactions with his accomplices' but no wallet addresses are provided. Detection should flag suspicious crypto activity patterns consistent with money laundering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cryptocurrency exchange API activity for suspicious patterns: rapid sequential deposits to wallets from different sources (fraud proceeds), immediate consolidation and transfers to mixing services, transaction volumes and frequency inconsistent with legitimate trading. Correlate exchange account registration times with breach timeframes and flag accounts with no prior history that suddenly activate during suspected fraud window.

suggestion.title: Malware Data Exfiltration and C2 Callback Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'transmitted them to servers controlled by the attackers' establishing C2 communication but pipeline generated zero detection for exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Infostealer callbacks typically occur at regular intervals (15-120 min). Flag repetitive HTTPS POST requests to non-standard ports (8000-8999, 9000-9999) from processes accessing credential stores. Detect high-entropy binary payloads in request bodies (encrypted/compressed stolen data). Baseline normal application traffic and alert on deviations: unexpected destinations, abnormal request sizes, timing patterns inconsistent with legitimate application behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Publishing Frequency Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article title promises coverage of '5 Supply Chain Attacks in 48 Hours'—all involve weaponized package uploads. Pipeline should detect sudden upload bursts to PyPI/npm/RubyGems from individual accounts within narrow time windows, with no prior publishing history.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single user accounts publishing 5+ packages or versions within 48 hours where prior 90-day publishing velocity is <1 per week. Correlate with newly-created GitHub accounts or accounts with recent credential exposure indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Modification
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via 'five attacks in 48 hours' context implies GitHub Actions abuse (common vector for credential exfiltration and downstream package injection). Pipeline should detect workflow.yml modifications introducing exfiltration logic or credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on additions of 'env:' blocks exporting secrets, 'curl' or 'wget' commands POSTing to non-GH domains, or 'uses:' references to unvetted actions. Baseline expected workflow complexity; flag novelty.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction in CI/CD Runner Environment
suggestion.rationale: Multi-attack article context suggests credential theft phase. Article phrase '5 attacks in 48 hours' implies parallel compromise—exfiltration of GitHub tokens, PyPI API keys, or npm credentials from action runner environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for environment variable enumeration (env, printenv, Get-Item env:) followed by outbound HTTP/S POST containing patterns matching GitHub token (ghp_), npm token (_auth base64), or PyPI API key prefixes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Forged Commit Metadata in Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks in rapid succession suggests actor is bulk-modifying repositories without proper code review. Article scope mentions 'why securing one layer is not enough'—implies bypass of branch protections and unsigned commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits merged to main/master branches by service accounts or newly-added collaborators where GPG signature verification is disabled, or where commit timestamps differ from push timestamps by >5 minutes (batch-created commits).

suggestion.title: Rapid Account Creation and Immediate Privilege Grant
suggestion.rationale: Five attacks in parallel timeline suggests infrastructure setup phase. Pipeline should flag bulk org/team membership changes immediately preceding malicious package publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accounts created within 24h of first malicious activity, immediately added to publishing-authorized teams, or granted admin scope tokens. Cross-reference with leaked credential feeds.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Secrets to External Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack definition includes data theft phase. Article context implies credential compromise; pipeline should detect outbound exfil of secrets to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/S POSTs to domains <7 days old, registered with privacy proxies, or with no HTTPS certificate history. Payload size >1KB + structure matching base64-encoded token formats. Correlate with CI/CD runner geolocation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes flaw that 'Enables Root Command Execution'—core attack is kernel-level privilege escalation. Pipeline produced zero detection for this primary technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged process spawning root-UID children without legitimate setuid/sudo invocation. Monitor for privilege boundary crossing via kernel syscall chains (clone/fork/execve). Flag processes with UID transition 0→non-root context restore.

suggestion.title: Root Command Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Root Command Execution'—the terminal impact. No detection for commands launched with UID=0 from unprivileged process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on command execution with effective UID=0 originating from non-root parent processes. Correlate process parentage and credential state across fork/exec boundaries.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Kernel Version Running Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability affecting 'Major Distros'—should enumerate affected kernel versions and create detection for systems running vulnerable releases. Pipeline provided zero version IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint kernel version via uname and compare against known-vulnerable ranges (9 years old suggests 2017-era kernel baseline). Alert on unpatched systems below fixed version threshold per distro.

suggestion.title: Kernel Panic / Crash Patterns from Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel flaws often leave traces in system logs during exploitation attempts—kernel panics, oops messages, or soft lockups. Article does not detail but pipeline should detect failure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel ring buffer (dmesg) and syslog for BUG, Oops, panic, or segfault signatures in context of suspicious privilege escalation. Correlate timing with process execution logs to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IIS Native Module Load or Registration
suggestion.rationale: BadIIS hijacks IIS servers—article title states 'hijacks IIS servers'—which requires installation of malicious IIS modules (.dll files) for persistence and code execution. Pipeline missed detection for T1505.004 (Server Software Component - IIS Module).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or suspicious .dll files written to IIS application directories (e.g., %SystemRoot%\System32\inetsrv\), registry writes to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\InetStp\Extensions, and w3wp.exe loading non-Microsoft modules via SetWindowsHookEx or rundll32.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Connections from w3wp.exe
suggestion.rationale: Malware that hijacks IIS and redirects users must exfiltrate data or receive C2 commands. Article title mentions 'redirect users to illicit sites'—implies C2 communication. Pipeline extracted no network IOCs or C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag w3wp.exe initiating outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations, especially on ports 80/443/8080. Correlate with DNS lookups for newly registered or suspicious domains. Monitor for HTTPS traffic without certificate pinning validation.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration or applicationHost.xml Modification
suggestion.rationale: HTTP redirection injection requires modification of IIS configuration files. Article explicitly states malware 'redirect[s] users to illicit sites'—requires configuration tampering. Pipeline did not surface detection for configuration modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to or modifications of %SystemRoot%\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.xml, web.config, and machine.config. Alert on non-Administrator process modifications or unexpected <rewrite> rule additions in IIS config.

suggestion.title: HTTP Response Header Injection or Body Rewrite via IIS
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking IIS to redirect users requires injecting or rewriting HTTP responses. Article says malware 'redirect users'—technical mechanism is response manipulation. Pipeline generated no detection for response-layer tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze IIS access logs for unusual Location or Refresh headers in HTTP responses, or 3xx redirect codes to unexpected domains. Monitor for injected script tags or frame redirects in text/html responses. Correlate with user complaints of unexpected site redirects.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IIS Application Pool Identity or Process Privilege Changes
suggestion.rationale: Malware persistence in IIS often requires elevation or privilege escalation. Article does not specify mechanism, but BadIIS campaigns typically escalate to SYSTEM or Local Service context. No privilege escalation detection UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IIS application pool identity changes to SYSTEM or NetworkService, or unexpected impersonation tokens in w3wp.exe. Alert on token impersonation calls via advapi32.dll from IIS worker processes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Obfuscated w3wp.exe Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Malware injected into IIS may spawn child processes for payload execution or reverse shells. Article title suggests active malicious redirection (not passive config injection)—implies runtime command execution. Pipeline did not generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned executables spawned by w3wp.exe, particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe without corresponding administrative context. Monitor for process hollowing or DLL injection indicators (e.g., CreateRemoteThread calls from IIS worker process).

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload API Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthorized API Access' as the attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface any authentication-related detection despite this being the core vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to Cisco Secure Workload API endpoints lacking valid Bearer tokens or using expired/revoked credentials. Spike in 401/403 responses followed by 200 success indicates credential brute-force or token enumeration. Track unusual source IPs or geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Cisco Secure Workload API Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Critical article about unauthorized API access implies credential theft or token abuse, but pipeline generated zero credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API tokens used from impossible-travel scenarios, off-hours, or non-standard User-Agent strings. Baseline normal API token holders (humans/services) and alert on token reuse outside those profiles. Monitor token creation frequency.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload Container Policy Discovery & Querying
suggestion.rationale: Post-authentication API abuse typically involves reconnaissance of container policies and security posture. Article mentions API access but pipeline missed discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag high-volume API queries to /policies, /containers, /rules, /members endpoints within short time window. Unusual service accounts or API tokens querying complete environment scans before any observed modification.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload API Configuration Changes by Unauthorized Caller
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access would logically lead to policy/rule manipulation for persistence or lateral movement. Pipeline generated zero impact/persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PUT/PATCH/DELETE operations on security policies, firewall rules, or RBAC settings by API tokens with no prior write history or from unexpected caller contexts. Flag whitelist/allowlist expansion suspicious in scope or timing.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload API Rate Limiting Bypass or Saturation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enabling 'unauthorized API access' may imply missing rate limits or auth enforcement. Pipeline should surface API abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal API request rates per token/user. Alert on sustained requests 10x+ baseline within rolling 5-min window without legitimate bulk operation context. Monitor for X-Forwarded-For header manipulation or request cycling across multiple API keys.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly concerns SQL injection vulnerability in Drupal core (CVE-2026-9082 per session context). Pipeline missed generating detection for SQL injection payloads targeting Drupal endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal default paths (/admin, /node, /user, /system) for SQL injection patterns: URL-encoded quotes, UNION SELECT, boolean-based payload markers (OR 1=1, AND 1=1), time-delay keywords (SLEEP, BENCHMARK, WAITFOR). Correlate with 400/403 response codes followed by 200/successful query patterns.

suggestion.title: Drupal Installation Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must first identify Drupal installation and version. Article title indicates vulnerability affects 'Drupal Core' — reconnaissance of version endpoints (CHANGELOG.txt, README.txt, /misc/drupal.js) is prerequisite exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Drupal version-disclosure endpoints: /CHANGELOG.txt, /README.txt, /sites/default/files, /web/sites/default/settings.php with 200 responses. Baseline normal Drupal admin access patterns and flag anomalous scanning (sequential requests to multiple standard Drupal paths in <60s window).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Query from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection vulnerability allows attacker to execute arbitrary database queries through web application. Should detect unexpected SQL patterns in database logs when initiated from web server process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for suspicious patterns originating from Drupal web process: UNION SELECT statements, information_schema queries, system table access (mysql.users, pg_shadow), data extraction into temporary tables, or queries with inline comment syntax (/* */, --). Baseline expected queries from application and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Drupal Default Path Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article concerns critical core vulnerability. Attackers enumerate vulnerable endpoint paths before exploitation. Common Drupal reconnaissance targets /admin/*, /user/*, /node/*, /modules/* paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of Drupal administrative and functional paths: >10 distinct requests to /admin/*, /user/login, /user/*, /modules/*, /themes/* with 40x responses from single source IP in <5 minute window. Correlate with user-agent consistency and lack of legitimate session cookies.

suggestion.title: Drupal Module Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection may be vector-specific (contributed module or core component). Detection should cover attempts to exploit known vulnerable Drupal components via parameter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: WAF/proxy detection: flag HTTP requests containing SQL keywords in query parameters commonly targeted in Drupal exploits (node ID parameters, search forms, exposed filter parameters). Target patterns: ?search=*, ?keys=*, ?field_*=* with SQL metacharacters. Cross-reference successful exploitation with subsequent large result-set downloads or slow query indicators.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Against Drupal Admin Panel
suggestion.rationale: Critical SQL injection may expose database; attackers often combine with credential compromise. Pre-exploitation phase includes attempts to brute-force /user/login or /admin/login endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor failed login attempts to Drupal default authentication endpoints (/user/login, /admin/login) for velocity anomalies: >5 failed attempts from single IP in <2 minutes, or >20 unique source IPs each with 1-3 failed attempts in <10 minute window. Correlate with successful SQL injection exploitation signals for multi-stage attack chain.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Nx Console Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension.' Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite explicit extension-based attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code extension installation from non-canonical marketplace or unsigned sources. Flag Nx Console v18.95.0 specifically. Alert on extension activation spawning suspicious child processes (node, curl, powershell) with file I/O to credential paths (~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, .env) within 60 seconds of install.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain trojan payloads execute post-install hooks enumerating credential stores. Article implies credential theft; pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm post-install script execution via node.exe; alert on child processes accessing credential files (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, Azure token cache) in rapid succession. Correlate with obfuscated JavaScript patterns (regex-based credential extraction, base64 encoding) in extension source code.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token & SSH Key Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached.' Trojan must harvest GitHub PATs and SSH keys. Pipeline did not surface credential-access phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process access to GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN environment variables or ~/.git-credentials files. Detect git config --global --list calls (credential enumeration) spawned by node/code.exe within Nx Console extension context. Flag rapid file reads of SSH private keys (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to TeamPCP C2
suggestion.rationale: Title implies repo breach; stolen credentials must exfil to attacker C2. Pipeline extracted no IOCs or exfiltration-phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT to known TeamPCP C2 domains with large JSON payloads (credential blobs). Alert on DNS queries for malware C2 IPs from developer machines post-npm-install. Correlate Azure token exfil patterns (large text strings, base64 tokens) to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen GitHub Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Once GitHub credentials stolen, attacker clones internal repos or pushes malicious code. Article explicitly states 'Internal Repositories Breached'; implies unauthorized git operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git clone/push operations using stolen credentials from anomalous IPs/geographies. Monitor for SSH key reuse to internal repos from attacker-controlled hosts. Detect multiple failed GitHub API auth attempts followed by successful access within 10 seconds (credential-stuffing pattern).

suggestion.title: Imposter Nx Console Package/Repository Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack relies on distributing trojanized Nx Console. Article likely describes fake marketplace entry or poisoned repository. Pipeline should surface hash-based and repository-signature IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare downloaded extension SHA256 hashes and git commit SHAs against canonical Nx GitHub and VSCode Marketplace. Alert on package installation from third-party mirrors or custom registries. Flag typosquatted package names (e.g., 'nxconsole', 'nx-console-pro') and unsigned extensions.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Malware Protection Engine Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies vulnerable versions '1.1.26030.3008 and earlier' and fixed version '1.1.26040.8'. Version inventory is an immediate, high-confidence detection anchor the pipeline should have generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender or WMI AntivirusProduct for Malware Protection Engine version and alert on any version < 1.1.26040.8. Correlate with patch deployment records to identify unpatched systems during CISA 2-week deadline window (through June 3).

suggestion.title: Antimalware Service Crash or Denial-of-Service State
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45498 explicitly 'trigger[s] denial-of-service (DoS) states on unpatched Windows devices'. Repeated crashes, hung processes, or service restart loops are the direct impact signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained Windows Event Log Event ID 1000 (application crash) for MpCmdRun.exe or mpengine.dll; monitor WinDefend (Windows Defender) service for restart loops (>3 restarts within 1 hour). Flag processes with abnormal CPU/memory consumption before service failure.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Link-Following in Defender Engine
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-41091 is 'improper link resolution before file access' allowing 'SYSTEM privileges'. Symlink/hardlink creation in Defender paths followed by privilege token elevation is the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sysmon Event 27 (file block executable) or ETW for symbolic link creation in C:\Program Files\Windows Defender or %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows Defender. Correlate with suspicious file access or abnormal child process spawning from non-System accounts, followed by token elevation to SYSTEM.

suggestion.title: Defender Engine Version Downgrade or Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit version verification guidance: 'update was successfully installed if the Malware Protection Platform version number... matches or exceeds the version number'. Version rollback or persistent mismatches during patching window indicate potential rollback attacks or missed deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline current Malware Protection Engine/Platform versions across fleet. Alert on any endpoint reporting version *lower* than its previous known version (rollback indicator) or deviating from org policy. Flag systems still running versions predating the CVE-2026-45498 fix (4.18.26030.3011 or earlier) after June 3 deadline.

suggestion.title: Active Exploitation Signal During Vulnerable Window
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerabilities are 'actively exploited in the wild' and CISA mandated emergency 2-week patching. Spikes in Defender crashes, service failures, or privilege escalation events during May 21–June 3 window correlate with active exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During May 21–June 3 window, correlate rising rates of WinDefend crashes, SYSTEM privilege escalations, and process isolation failures across unpatched endpoints. Alert on geographic or time-clustered anomalies suggesting coordinated exploitation campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credential Store Access from Non-Standard Process
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates multiple coordinated supply chain attacks. Context mentions Nx Console trojan extracting GitHub tokens, npm credentials, AWS keys, SSH keys, and 1Password secrets. Detection gap: unauthorized reads from ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npm, ~/.config/gh directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-package-manager processes access known credential store paths in rapid succession. Correlate file access to process parent (IDE extension, Python script) and compare to baseline credential manager behavior.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Version Deployment to Repository
suggestion.rationale: Title references '5 attacks in 48 hours' in supply chain context. Context shows npm/PyPI compromises. Detection gap: rapid version deployments, unusual metadata signatures, or pre-release versions from compromised maintainer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository APIs for single-account version uploads within 48-hour window, especially if version downgrades or major dependency changes. Flag if file hashes diverge from expected build artifacts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LaunchAgent/Persistence Artifact Creation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks require persistence. Context shows Nx Console deployed ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist. Detection gap: obfuscated daemon names installed to persistence directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on plist/cron creation with animal/system-utility codenames (kitty, gh, update, monitor) in LaunchAgents or ~/.local. Correlate file creation to IDE extension or package manager process ancestry.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Package Manager API (GitHub/npm/PyPI)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies coordinated exfiltration across 5 attacks. Context shows use of GitHub Search API and npm registry for command channels. Detection gap: high-frequency API calls with credential/repository enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes making sustained API calls to package repositories outside standard package manager binaries. Flag iterative query patterns (walk repos, enumerate secrets), unusual search terms, or bulk downloads from single-use tokens.

suggestion.title: IDE Extension Installation from Non-Standard Source
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions '5 attacks in 48 hours.' Context shows Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension compromised, remained on marketplace 18 minutes. Detection gap: extension version downgrades, sideloaded installations, or registry manifest mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code/JetBrains extension installations where (a) version is lower than installed, (b) manifest hash mismatches published registry, or (c) installation occurs via non-marketplace URL or offline vsix with obfuscated setup code.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Build/Package Tool Execution with Hidden Setup
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks leverage developer workflow tools. Nx Console trojan disguised payload as MCP setup. Detection gap: tools executing hidden initialization code during installation or first-run.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawned child processes with no parent console interaction (silent execution) during IDE extension activation or package tool installation. Correlate to unusual network egress (GitHub API, DNS tunneling) or credential file opens.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Upload to Webroot
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'BadIIS Malware Turns Hijacks IIS Servers' — web shell deployment to wwwroot or vti_bin is the standard execution vector for IIS compromise. No detection UC generated despite this being the explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file creation in IIS directories (wwwroot, vti_bin, aspnet_client) with extensions .asp, .aspx, .php, .txt, .config. Correlate with W3SVC process access and anomalous HTTP POST requests within minutes of file creation. Alert on base64 or hex-encoded script payloads in uploaded files.

suggestion.title: IIS Module and Handler Injection Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hijacks IIS servers' and 'redirect users' — BadIIS achieves persistence via rogue httpModule or notification handler injection in ApplicationHost.config. No UC addresses IIS metabase or handler chain tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W3SVC\Parameters and %WINDIR%\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config for new module or handler entries. Alert on non-Microsoft module CLSIDs, new assembly loads by w3wp.exe, or appcmd.exe invocations without change-management tickets. Baseline legitimate IIS modules and alert on additions.

suggestion.title: HTTP Traffic Redirection from IIS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'redirect users to illicit sites' — BadIIS injects HTTP 302/307 responses or modifies Location headers to redirect legitimate traffic. No detection UC covers response-header hijacking or outbound redirection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse IIS logs for unusual 302/307 Location headers pointing to newly registered or suspicious domains. Identify outbound connections from w3wp.exe to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially on uncommon ports (8080, 8888, non-standard 443). Correlate with Domain Reputation feeds for known malvertising domains.

suggestion.title: Anomalous w3wp.exe Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Web shells spawn cmd.exe, PowerShell, certutil, or rundll32 as children of application pool identity. Article's 'hijack' implies interactive post-exploitation requiring process execution. No UC generated for w3wp process spawning suspicious children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, certutil.exe, or bitsadmin.exe. Monitor for base64 arguments, file downloads via curl/wget, or registry modifications initiated from application pool identity. Establish per-pool baseline and alert on deviations. Check parent-child chain integrity.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from IIS-Hosted Malware
suggestion.rationale: Session context identifies 'malware-as-a-service' (obs. 1304). MaaS campaigns require C2 callback infrastructure. No UC covers outbound C2 communication or operator callbacks from compromised IIS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe for outbound TCP/UDP to non-whitelisted ASNs, especially on non-standard ports (8080, 4444, 9090). Detect periodic beaconing intervals (300s, 600s, 3600s). Cross-reference domains against TI feeds for known BadIIS C2 infrastructure. Alert on HTTPS without cert pinning or self-signed certificates.

suggestion.title: ApplicationHost.config and Registry Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: BadIIS modifies system configuration for persistent access. Article describes capability to 'hijack' — implies config-level control. No UC addresses registry or IIS config file modifications as persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement file integrity monitoring on %WINDIR%\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config with alert on modifications outside maintenance windows. Monitor registry writes to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W3SVC by non-SYSTEM accounts. Alert on IIS configuration changes without corresponding MSI or OS update events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco Secure Workload API Access from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Enables Unauthorized API Access'—expect detection of unauthenticated or misauthenticated API calls to Cisco Workload endpoints. Pipeline extracted nothing despite this being the core vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Secure Workload API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/*, /vulnerability-*) originating from non-whitelisted external IPs or missing/invalid Bearer tokens. Flag 401/403 response codes followed by successful 200s from same source within minutes (token brute-force or bypass).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Token/Session Manipulation in Cisco Secure Workload APIs
suggestion.rationale: API authentication bypass typically involves token forgery or session hijacking. Article phrase 'Enables Unauthorized API Access' implies authentication layer bypass—pipeline should detect anomalous auth patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed API authentication attempts followed by successful requests using modified/replayed tokens. Monitor for token claims with unexpected privilege levels or issuer mismatches in JWT payloads (if applicable to Cisco platform).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Cisco Secure Workload API Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Critical API vulnerability often leads to reconnaissance of other workload services. Article severity 'critical' suggests blast radius beyond single API endpoint—expect follow-on enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple reconnaissance-pattern API calls within short time window: HEAD requests to /api/*/status, /health, /version endpoints; requests to non-existent endpoints returning 404 (fuzzing); rapid sequential requests to multiple /workload/* URIs from same source IP or user context.

suggestion.title: Drupal Exploitation Attempt Detection via URI Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Critical Drupal Core Security Vulnerability' and standard Drupal vulns are exploited via specific URI paths (admin/*, ?q=*, etc.). Pipeline failed to extract exploitation patterns. This is T1190 initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs (IIS, Apache, Nginx) for HTTP requests targeting known Drupal exploitation URIs (e.g., /admin/*, /user/*, /install.php, ?q=, /xmlrpc.php). Pair with POST methods and non-standard User-Agent strings to detect automated exploit frameworks.

suggestion.title: Drupal Web Shell Upload & File Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Drupal vulnerabilities often lead to webroot file write (T1505.004). Pipeline missed detection for file system changes in docroot/sites/default/files or module directories where shells commonly hide.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation in Drupal-sensitive directories (/sites/default/files, /modules, /themes, /includes) with executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .inc). Correlate with process execution from www-data/apache user spawning cmd/bash.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database Access from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation often involves attacker database queries via web shell. Pipeline missed detection for SQL query patterns from httpd/nginx process. Article context suggests data compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database access logs for queries originating from web application process (www-data, IUSR, apache). Flag unusual SELECT statements targeting user credentials, node content, or system tables from non-standard connection origins.

suggestion.title: Drupal Module/Extension Installation Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attacker-uploaded malicious modules are common post-exploit behavior. Article does not specify which module/core component is vulnerable, but pipeline should detect unauthorized module installation or updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file system writes to /modules or /themes directories outside of scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on drush or composer process execution with install/update arguments running as web user. Baseline legitimate update processes first.

suggestion.title: Drupal Admin Account Creation or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers commonly create admin accounts post-exploitation. Pipeline missed database-level detection for user table modifications with admin role assignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal user table for unexpected INSERT/UPDATE operations granting admin role (uid=1, role=administrator). Correlate with web shell process execution timestamps. Cross-reference against change control ticket audit.

suggestion.title: Drupal Log Tampering & Debug Mode Activation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often disable logging or enable debug mode to hide tracks. Pipeline missed detection for configuration changes to settings.php or log deletion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to settings.php, .htaccess, or web server config that disable logging or error reporting. Monitor for deletion of watchdog table or access to /var/log/drupal-* outside of log rotation windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation from Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes attack vector: 'Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension' — indicates supply chain compromise of dev tooling that auto-loads on startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.vscode/extensions/ and %APPDATA%\Code\User\extensions for suspicious extension installations, particularly those with version mismatches or modified package.json. Cross-reference installed extension versions against known malicious versions (e.g., @nxext/nx-console 18.95.0). Alert on extension auto-load hooks modified outside of legitimate VS Code update mechanisms.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Exfiltration via Compromised IDE Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates breach of internal GitHub repos, implying credential theft. Extensions with user context can access ~/.ssh/github.com and credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual file access patterns where VS Code extension processes read from ~/.ssh/, ~/.git-credentials, or environment variable injection points containing GITHUB_TOKEN. Correlate with outbound DNS/HTTP to unknown C2 domains. Watch for child processes spawned by code.exe or Code.exe attempting credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Version Anomaly in Dev Dependency Trees
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages @nxext/nx-console v18.95.0 malicious package version. Detection should flag unexpected version pinning or hash mismatches in lock files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package-lock.json / yarn.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml version hashes against npm registry canonical hashes. Alert on version downgrades or hash mismatches for critical dev dependencies. Monitor npm install/ci execution for non-zero exit codes followed by successful silencing or retry.

suggestion.title: Imposter Git Commit Signature Spoofing in Repository Pushes
suggestion.rationale: Prior context (obs. 1288) identifies 68 imposter commit SHAs across actions-cool repositories. Detection should identify commits with fabricated signatures or mismatched committer metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit git log for commits with: (1) committer name/email matching legitimate developers but signature verification failures; (2) commit SHAs that match known spoofed commits; (3) commits authored during off-hours by users with no prior history of commits at those times. Correlate with actor IP geolocations.

suggestion.title: Extension Runtime Privilege Escalation and Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: VS Code extensions run with full user privilege context and can access secrets, environment variables, and network—establishing a lateral movement vector post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor code.exe/Code.exe child process spawning—particularly powershell.exe, cmd.exe, curl.exe, or wget.exe launched from extension directories. Alert on subprocess invocation of credential dumping tools (printenv, env, Get-ChildItem env:*). Detect outbound HTTP/S connections from extension processes to non-whitelisted domains with base64/URL-encoded payloads in request bodies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Tag-Spoofing Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Prior context (obs. 1286, 1288) describes GitHub Actions tag-spoofing exploiting in-memory credential harvest from CI/CD runners—actions-cool repository as delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow execution for: (1) uses: statements referencing actions-cool/* repositories with unexpected commit SHAs; (2) environment variable injection of GITHUB_TOKEN into unvetted action steps; (3) workflow runs spawning credential enumeration subprocesses (git config credential.helper, aws sts get-caller-identity). Alert on credential exfiltration patterns (curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer' to external URLs).

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in Web Application Layer to RCE
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Exposes PostgreSQL Sites to RCE'—core vector is SQL injection permitting command execution within database context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web logs for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, INSERT, EXEC, pg_*) in query parameters, URL-encoded payloads, or POST bodies targeting Drupal endpoints. Detect SQLi signature patterns such as OR/AND logic injection, time-delay probes, and comment-based injection (-- , #, /**/).

suggestion.title: Database Process Spawning Shell Commands
suggestion.rationale: RCE via database exploit typically chains SQL injection → COPY/EXEC to spawn system shells. Article title implies this progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect postgres/mysql/web-app service account spawning bash, cmd.exe, or powershell processes. Alert on unexpected child processes from apache/nginx/php-fpm. Correlate with database query logs showing COPY TO PROGRAM or similar execution directives.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core Module/Configuration File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Drupal core vulnerabilities often lead to unauthorized .module file writes or settings.php injection. Article mentions 'core flaw'—implies file-system compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal root directory and /modules for unexpected file creation/modification by web-app account. Alert on suspicious .module, .php, or .inc file writes post-deployment. Correlate with POST requests to /admin paths or Drupal API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Abnormal PostgreSQL Authentication from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Exploit chains database credential theft or unauthorized re-authentication. Detecting failed/successful auth spikes from web app context surfaces compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track PostgreSQL connection attempts from web-app service account. Alert on: (1) auth failures followed by success within <5sec; (2) connections to non-standard databases; (3) simultaneous connections to >3 databases from single app PID.

suggestion.title: Drupal Update/Patch Mechanism Bypassed or Delayed
suggestion.rationale: Critical 'core flaw' implies time-window where unpatched instances remain vulnerable. Monitor patch failure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed or blocked Drupal update attempts (drush updb failures, composer update errors). Alert when security patch timestamp is older than vulnerability disclosure by >7 days. Flag disabled automated updates or permission denials on core/modules directories.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Encoding/Obfuscation Targeting Drupal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection payloads often URL-encoded, base64, or hex-encoded to evade WAF/IDS. Drupal-specific endpoints (admin, user, node) are high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for requests to /admin*, /user/login, /node/*, /api/* endpoints containing %2527, %2528 (encoded quotes/parens), base64 blobs, or hex strings in query/POST. Correlate with subsequent 200 responses or database errors.

suggestion.title: Defender Process Injection and Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerabilities are 'actively exploited'—implies post-exploitation privilege escalation. Expected detection for abnormal MsMpEng.exe or Sense.exe child process spawning, token manipulation, or WinDefend service tampering patterns following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by MsMpEng.exe or Sense.exe (normally isolated). Detect registry modifications to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinDefend startup parameters or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender disabling features. Flag access token impersonation attempts immediately following Defender process anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE Exploitation Against Microsoft Defender Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies two CVEs with active exploitation. Expected IOC extraction of CVE identifiers and detection rules for vulnerability-specific exploitation signatures, shellcode injection targeting MsMpEng.exe or Sense.exe, or abnormal API sequences (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection attempts targeting Defender components. Alert on LoadLibrary/GetProcAddress chains followed by WriteProcessMemory against Defender processes. Flag execution of files from %TEMP% or %APPDATA% that subsequently spawn Defender-related processes with suspicious parent-child lineage.

suggestion.title: Defender Antimalware Monitoring Disabled or Modified
suggestion.rationale: Defender vulnerability enables post-exploitation defense evasion. Expected use case for detecting security feature disablement via registry modification, WMI property changes, or Set-MpPreference cmdlet abuse to suppress detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinDefend registry path for DisableMonitoring=1 or Start parameter changes from 2 (auto) to 3/4 (manual/disabled). Alert on Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring commands. Detect removal of WinDefend service ACLs or tampering with event channel logging for Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender.

suggestion.title: PyPI Poisoned Package Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'supply chain attacks in 48 hours'—PyPI compromises (LiteLLM, durabletask) are primary attack surface; pipeline produced zero UCs despite this obvious vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package uploads to PyPI with unusual metadata (mismatched source hash, bloated binary vs. published source), uploads from newly-created or low-reputation accounts, or packages with suspicious external dependencies injected at publish time. Correlate against known threat actor aliases (TeamPCP, etc.).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Tag Spoofing & Imposter Action Creation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain context implies GitHub-hosted attack vectors (Actions tag hijacking, lookalike action namespaces); article likely describes this pattern but pipeline surfaced zero detection cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of GitHub Actions matching established patterns (setup-*, actions-cool-*, build-*) from accounts without prior Actions publishing history, or Actions added to repos seconds before a high-privilege CI/CD run.

suggestion.title: Malicious IDE Extension Installation from Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Nx Console v18.95.0 credential-stealer campaign (noted in session context) suggests IDE extension supply chain is an attack vector; no UCs generated despite likely article discussion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code/JetBrains extension installations from unsigned publishers, extensions bearing typosquatted names of popular tools (nx-console vs. nx-consol), or extensions that spawn processes accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or credential stores immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Git Commit Hash Spoofing & Tree Confusion Attack
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks manipulate commit SHAs to evade CI/CD verification; article context mentions '68 imposter commit SHAs'—this is a concrete attack step the pipeline ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits with identical or near-collision SHAs from different authors, commits with valid signatures but mismatched tree hashes, or high volumes of commits to ci/ or .github/workflows/ directories from newly-onboarded maintainers.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Artifact-Source Divergence
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned packages hide malicious code in published artifacts while keeping source clean; article context implies this evasion, but no detection for it was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare published package bytecode/dependencies against published source; alert on size mismatches >10%, presence of binary artifacts not in source tree, or dependencies listed in lockfile but absent from published package.json.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Package Lifecycle Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attackers abuse npm/pip lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, setup.py) to steal CI/CD tokens; core attack pattern that pipeline should surface but did not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning during package installation (npm, pip, pnpm install), particularly curl/wget/PowerShell processes reaching external domains or base64-encoded command execution, and correlation with environment variables containing TOKEN, SECRET, or AWS_.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Elevation to Root via Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Root Command Execution on Major Distros.' This is the primary attack outcome—detecting processes spawning with root euid from non-root parent. No UC generated despite being the core indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of shell (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or system utilities with euid=0 from unprivileged parent process, especially across glibc/kernel-level syscalls without sudo/su context. Kernel LPE exploits typically fork with root privs post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Setuid Binary Execution Chain During Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits typically chain through setuid binaries (/usr/bin/sudo, /bin/ping, /sbin/ip) as elevation vector; title's 'root command execution' implies setuid abuse but pipeline missed T1548.004 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of setuid-enabled binaries by unprivileged users that spawn unexpected child processes or trigger unusual syscalls. Correlate with memory operations (mmap, mprotect) indicative of exploit staging.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Kernel Syscall Sequence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits are distinguished by syscall patterns (ptrace, prctl, mmap race conditions); article describes 9-year-old kernel flaw but provides no technical detail. Syscall-level detection is table-stakes for kernel LPE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal syscall sequences per binary using eBPF. Flag anomalies: rapid ptrace/prctl chains, mmap followed by code execution, mlock/madvise operations preceding privilege escalation, or timing patterns consistent with race-condition exploitation.

suggestion.title: Process Capability/Credential Elevation Outside Authorization Paths
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits grant capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE) or modify task credentials (setuid syscall). Article title implies root access; no detection UC addresses capability grants or credential changes outside PAM/sudo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor auditctl for process credential changes (setuid, setfsgid, cap_setpcap) not triggered via sudo, su, or PAM. Flag unexpected CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_ADMIN grants to unprivileged processes.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Spawning Suspicious Children
suggestion.rationale: Article describes BadIIS 'hijacks IIS servers'—malware injection into w3wp.exe worker processes is standard IIS compromise technique. No behavioral detection suggested despite explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe spawning child processes outside expected AppPool behavior (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, curl.exe). IIS malware typically executes commands via process injection or service spawning. Correlate with unusual network activity from IIS.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration Modification (applicationHost.config)
suggestion.rationale: BadIIS hijacking requires modifying IIS configuration to persist or route requests. Article mentions 'redirect users' but no detection for config tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config, urlRewrite.config, or web.config outside change-control windows. Track filesystem operations and timestamp anomalies on IIS config directories.

suggestion.title: IIS Module Registration and DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: IIS malware persistence commonly uses native module registration. No detection suggested for DLL loading into IIS process space despite 'hijacks' language implying code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned DLLs loaded into w3wp.exe, especially from user-writable paths or IIS directories. Track new module entries in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\InetStp\Components. Watch for requests to non-existent modules in IIS logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound HTTP Connections from w3wp.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'redirect users to illicit sites'—implies C2 communication or redirect infrastructure. No detection for command-and-control or external beaconing from IIS process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate outbound connections from w3wp.exe (typically none or limited to app backends). Alert on new external IPs/domains, non-standard ports, or high-frequency requests from IIS worker processes. Correlate with IIS access logs.

suggestion.title: HTTP Response Header Manipulation and URL Rewriting
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'redirect users to illicit sites.' Pipeline missed detection for HTTP header injection or IIS URL Rewrite rules insertion without authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect IIS access logs and HTTP response headers for injected Location, Refresh, or X-Redirect headers not matching domain allowlist. Monitor URL Rewrite rule additions via IIS Manager audit logs or registry. Baseline expected redirect patterns by site.

suggestion.title: IIS Service Account Privilege Escalation and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking requires compromising or escalating IIS service account context. No detection for account manipulation, lateral movement from IIS host, or SAM/LSASS access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IIS service account (typically IUSR, ApplicationPoolIdentity, or custom accounts) performing privilege escalation, accessing SAM/LSASS, or initiating lateral movement via SMB. Monitor for unexpected domain enumeration queries from IIS host.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via fltMC.exe and FLTLIB.dll
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'it starts with the execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure (fltMC.exe + FLTLIB.dll)'. This is the Windows execution vector that precedes JFMBackdoor payload loading and is a critical detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for fltMC.exe process creation with parent process being batch script execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Correlate with unusual FLTLIB.dll file writes to system directories. Flag if fltMC.exe loads FLTLIB.dll from non-standard paths or recently-created DLL files.

suggestion.title: Service Creation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'establish persistence via a new service'. Showboat explicitly uses service registration as persistence mechanism but no specifics are provided in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sc.exe or PowerShell service creation commands on Linux/Windows systems (particularly telecom-adjacent networks). Alert on service registration pointing to unusual paths, especially /tmp or world-writable directories.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy and Port Forwarding Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Its most notable function is acting as a SOCKS5 proxy and port-forwarding pivot point, serving as a foothold on compromised endpoints and enabling the attackers to move to other systems on the internal network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5 proxy traffic patterns (SOCKS protocol handshake bytes 0x05) from single-purpose hosts toward multiple internal IP ranges. Flag unusual port-forwarding activity or netstat entries showing listening SOCKS5 ports on compromised systems with no legitimate business justification.

suggestion.title: External Code Retrieval from Pastebin for Process Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the hide command, which enables a process to conceal itself on a host machine by retrieving code stored on external websites such as Pastebin or online forums for use as a dead drop'. Direct evasion technique using web-hosted payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Pastebin and similar paste sites (raw.githubusercontent.com, dpaste, etc.) originating from unexpected systems, particularly servers. Correlate with process hiding or code injection signals. Flag DNS queries to pastebin.com or related services followed by file writes to /tmp or process descriptor manipulation.

suggestion.title: Batch Script Execution Dropping JFMBackdoor Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Windows attack chain: 'it starts with the execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure'. This is initial execution vector for Windows variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or batch script execution with suspicious child processes (powershell, certutil, bitsadmin). Alert on batch scripts dropping files to temp directories or system paths, especially multiple sequential file writes within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture with Encryption for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: JFMBackdoor capability: 'Screenshot capture — Take screenshots of the victim's desktop and encrypt them for exfiltration'. Collection and exfiltration of sensitive visual data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for screenshot-capture APIs (BitBlt, GetDC) invoked by non-graphical processes or unusual process parents. Flag processes accessing graphics subsystems from system service contexts or unusual accounts. Correlate with file creation in temp directories followed by encryption key material usage.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco Secure Workload API Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthorized API Access'—pipeline should detect authentication bypass or credential abuse against Secure Workload API endpoints. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API authentication failures followed by successful requests without credential re-entry, or authentication from non-whitelisted IP ranges. Flag Bearer token reuse across geographically disparate locations within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Secure Workload Policies and Workgroups via API
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access would immediately enable discovery—attacker enumerates microsegmentation policies, workgroups, and network topology. Title establishes access but pipeline missed discovery phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume API queries to /policies, /workgroups, /agents endpoints in short time window. Threshold: >50 enumeration calls per API token per 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Secure Workload API Token
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains API access ('Unauthorized API Access'), they pivot within the environment using valid tokens to modify policies, onboard rogue agents, or create exfiltration paths. No lateral movement UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track API calls that modify policy enforcement (PUT /policies), add agents (POST /agents), or change workgroup membership. Flag calls originating from untrusted networks. Correlate with subsequent suspicious intra-network traffic.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Secure Workload Configuration Changes via API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Unauthorized API Access' without boundary; attacker can modify policies, bypass segmentation, disable monitoring. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls that delete policies (DELETE /policies), disable agent reporting, or modify enforcement levels. Cross-reference with absence of change-request tickets in ITSM system.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Secure Workload API Metadata Access
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access includes access to workload metadata, traffic telemetry, and policy rules—all usable for targeting. Pipeline missed exfiltration-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API exports (GET /analytics/traffic, GET /workloads/manifest) with large response payloads. Flag data export via API to external IPs or S3 URLs embedded in API responses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Client User-Agent or SDK Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits an API authentication flaw—attacker likely uses malformed or non-standard client headers, or scripted API abuse. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API requests from non-standard User-Agents (custom scripts, curl, Postman, Burp), API requests missing expected SDK signatures, or requests with malformed Authorization headers (missing 'Bearer', expired tokens, invalid encodings).

suggestion.title: Drupal Web Application Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Critical Drupal Core Security Vulnerability Exposes Websites to Cyberattack'—establishes web exploitation vector. Pipeline must detect reconnaissance and exploitation of Drupal admin/REST endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal-specific paths (/admin, /rest, /user, /sites/default) with suspicious payloads—SQL keywords, encoded PHP, or GET parameter counts exceeding baselines. Flag non-browser User-Agents targeting Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Remote Code Execution via Unsafe Handler Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'cyberattack exposure' from critical vulnerability; Drupal Core RCE is standard attack pattern. Pipeline should have generated code-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by web server daemon (apache, nginx, php-fpm). Alert on execution of shells, compilers, or interpreters from Drupal theme/module directories. Monitor for eval() or system() calls in application context.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Query Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Drupal Core vulnerabilities manifest as SQL injection (observation 1305: CVE-2026-9082 Drupal SQL Injection). Pipeline should have flagged SQL injection detection given Drupal software context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for UNION-based injection syntax (UNION SELECT), time-based delays (SLEEP()), or comment obfuscation (/*!, --, #) originating from web application user. Alert on queries to information_schema or system tables from Drupal context.

suggestion.title: Drupal Authentication Bypass or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability may bypass authentication or elevate privileges. Title signals 'cyberattack exposure'; pipeline must detect unauthorized admin access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful logins to Drupal /admin without valid credentials, rapid user role elevation (user → admin), session token creation anomalies, or admin actions from non-whitelisted IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title directly states 'Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension' as attack vector. Should detect extension installation with suspicious network/credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension marketplace installations and post-install behavior. Flag extensions with suspicious process spawning, credential/SSH key access, or outbound connections to non-standard hosts within 60s of activation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credential Access from Development Tool Context
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates breach of GitHub 'internal repositories,' implying credential/token theft. Extension execution should precede credential enumeration (git config, SSH keys, environment variables).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code process or child processes reading ~/.ssh, .git/config, or environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, GIT_SSH_KEY. Alert on bulk reads of credential stores within extension execution context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Operations from IDE Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Breach of internal repos suggests attacker-driven git commands (clone, push, credential enumeration). Extension should not spawn git with unusual argument patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git child processes spawned by VS Code/extension with non-standard arguments: git credential fill, git config --list (especially credential.helper enumeration), or git clone/push to unfamiliar remotes.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of GitHub SSH Keys / PATs
suggestion.rationale: Title states breach of GitHub repos; typical follow-on is outbound exfil of credentials to C2. Extension code should not initiate unexpected network connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VS Code or extension child processes making outbound connections to non-development-tool domains, especially with subsequent HTTP POST payloads containing base64-encoded keys or token patterns.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Credential Theft from VS Code
suggestion.rationale: GitHub repos breach implies theft of CI/CD tokens, SSH keys stored as env vars. Extension has access to parent process env and can exfil via DNS/HTTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension child processes for env var enumeration (printenv, env command) or process memory reads targeting strings matching GITHUB, SSH, TOKEN, KEY patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Marketplace Distribution of Nx Console Extension
suggestion.rationale: Attack depends on users downloading poisoned Nx Console from VS Code marketplace. Should detect version anomalies, rapid version churn, or marketplace availability gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension marketplace requests and installation events. Flag installations of Nx Console v18.95.0 or versions with unusual hash mismatches, rapid re-releases, or withdrawn-then-republished packages.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Phishing Site Hosting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Affiliates provide traffic through phishing links, fake websites' and 'website-cloning feature that allowed affiliates to clone phishing pages and receive ZIP files preloaded with the latest Lucifer code.' No UC generated for detecting phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains with crypto/NFT/DeFi keywords matching legitimate platforms (uniswap, opensea, airdrop) deployed under known affiliate hosting providers. Correlate high-velocity subdomain creation and SSL certificate issuance. Alert on phishing-kit ZIP file downloads from C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Wallet ERC20 Approve & Permit2 Transaction Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ERC20 support, Permit2 abuse, off-chain signatures' as Lucifer features enabling execution. 'Once permission is granted, the drainer can automatically transfer tokens...often within seconds.' No UC for malicious wallet approvals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ERC20 approve()/Permit() transactions to unknown spender contracts from victim wallets. Flag rapid approve → transfer() patterns within 60 seconds. Correlate approval events with phishing domain access logs. Monitor Permit2 contract interactions from unverified dApp origins.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Zero Config Affiliate Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Zero Config deployment workflows, allowing affiliates to upload static files, automatically generate phishing-ready packages, and deploy infrastructure with minimal manual work.' Pipeline missed automated deployment infrastructure UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP downloads containing drainer payload templates from C2. Identify automated deployment signatures: static file uploads followed by rapid site generation, certificate provisioning, and DNS propagation cycles. Flag command-line patterns for Lucifer build/deploy tooling.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Telegram C2 Coordination & Hit Notifications
